sentences.zh: 王敦

translations.literal: Wang Dun.
translations.idiomatic: This biography concerns Wang Dun.

sentences.zh: 王敦，字處仲，司徒導之從父兄也。

translations.literal: Wang Dun, styled Chuzhong, was the older paternal cousin of Minister of Education Wang Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun, whose courtesy name was Chuzhong, stood to Wang Dao—the future Minister of Education—as an elder cousin on the Wang line.

sentences.zh: 父基，治書侍御史。

translations.literal: His father Wang Ji served as Supervising Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Wang Ji, had held the post of Supervising Secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 敦少有奇人之目，尚武帝女襄城公主，拜駙馬都尉，除太子舍人。

translations.literal: From youth Dun had the reputation of an extraordinary man; he married Emperor Wu's daughter Princess Xiangcheng, was appointed Commandant of the Household for the Imperial Son-in-Law, and was given the office of Gentleman Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a young man Wang Dun was marked as exceptional; he married Princess Xiangcheng, a daughter of Emperor Wu, received the title of commandant for the imperial son-in-law's household, and was made a gentleman attendant at the heir apparent's palace.

sentences.zh: 時王愷、石崇以豪侈相尚，愷嘗置酒，敦與導俱在坐，有女伎吹笛小失聲韻，愷便驅殺之，一坐改容，敦神色自若。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Kai and Shi Chong vied in extravagant luxury. Once when Kai held a banquet, both Dun and Dao were among the guests. A female musician playing the flute made a slight slip in tone, and Kai immediately had her driven off and killed. The whole company changed color; Dun's expression remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kai and Shi Chong were famous for trying to outspend each other. At one of Kai's feasts Wang Dun and Wang Dao were present when a flute-player missed a note; Kai had her killed on the spot. The guests blanched; Wang Dun never flinched.

sentences.zh: 他日，又造愷，愷使美人行酒，以客飲不盡，輒殺之。

translations.literal: On another day he again visited Kai. Kai had beauties pass the wine, and whenever a guest did not finish his cup, he killed the beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Another time Wang Dun called on Kai, who sent serving girls to pour wine—if a guest left his cup unfinished, Kai executed the girl who had served him.

sentences.zh: 酒至敦、導所，敦故不肯持，美人悲懼失色，而敦傲然不視。

translations.literal: When the wine reached Dun and Dao, Dun deliberately would not take his cup; the beauty was stricken with grief and fear and lost color, yet Dun looked on haughtily and paid no attention.
translations.idiomatic: When the cup came to Wang Dun and Wang Dao, Dun deliberately refused it; the girl wept and turned pale with terror, while Dun stared past her with cold indifference.

sentences.zh: 導素不能飲，恐行酒者得罪，遂勉強盡觴。

translations.literal: Dao ordinarily could not drink; fearing the wine-server would be punished, he forced himself to empty his cup.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao could barely hold his liquor; afraid the server would pay with her life, he drained his cup despite himself.

sentences.zh: 導還，歎曰：「處仲若當世，心懷剛忍，非令終也。

translations.literal: Dao returned and sighed, saying, "If Chuzhong comes to dominate the age, he cherishes a hard, cruel heart—he will not end well."
translations.idiomatic: Back home Wang Dao sighed, "If Chuzhong ever rules the times, his ruthlessness will undo him—he will not die in his bed."

sentences.zh: 」洗馬潘滔見敦而目之曰：「處仲蜂目已露，但豺聲未振，若不噬人，亦當為人所噬。

translations.literal: " Cavalier Attendant Pan Tao saw Dun and sized him up, saying, "Chuzhong's 'wasp eyes' are already showing, but the 'jackal voice' has not yet sounded; if he does not devour others, he will yet be devoured by others."
translations.idiomatic: Palace groom Pan Tao studied Wang Dun and said, "Chuzhong already has the eyes of a wasp; the jackal's cry has not sounded. Either he devours others, or others will devour him."

sentences.zh: 」及太子遷許昌，詔東宮官屬不得送。

translations.literal: " When the heir apparent was moved to Xuchang, an edict forbade Eastern Palace officials from escorting him.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was relocated to Xuchang, the court ordered that no staff from the Eastern Palace might accompany him.

sentences.zh: 敦及洗馬江統、潘滔，舍人杜蕤、魯瑤等，冒禁于路側望拜流涕，時論稱之。

translations.literal: Dun together with Grooms Jiang Tong and Pan Tao, Attendants Du Rui and Lu Yao, and others, violated the prohibition and waited by the roadside to bow and weep; opinion of the day praised them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun, together with the grooms Jiang Tong and Pan Tao and the attendants Du Rui and Lu Yao, broke the ban, lined the road to bow and weep, and won praise across the capital.

sentences.zh: 遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫篡位，敦叔父彥為兗州刺史，倫遣敦慰勞之。

translations.literal: When Prince of Zhao Sima Lun usurped the throne, Dun's uncle Yan was Governor of Yan Province; Lun sent Dun to console him.
translations.idiomatic: During Prince Zhao's coup, Wang Dun's uncle Wang Yan governed Yan Province; Sima Lun dispatched Wang Dun to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 會諸王起義兵；

translations.literal: It happened that the princes raised armies in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Then the imperial princes rose in arms.

sentences.zh: 彥被齊王冏檄，懼倫兵強，不敢應命，敦勸彥起兵應諸王，故彥遂立勳績。

translations.literal: Yan had received a summons from Prince of Qi Sima Jiong; fearing Lun's forces were strong, he dared not obey. Dun urged Yan to raise troops in answer to the princes, so Yan was able to establish merit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan had been summoned by the Prince of Qi, Sima Jiong, but feared Sima Lun's strength and hesitated. Wang Dun persuaded him to march in support of the allied princes, and Yan thereby earned distinction.

sentences.zh: 惠帝反正，敦遷散騎常侍、左衛將軍、大鴻臚、侍中，出除廣武將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui was restored, Dun was promoted to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of the Left Guards, Grand Master of Guests, and Palace Attendant; he was then sent out as General Who Spreads Might and Governor of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Hui was returned to the throne, Wang Dun rose through cavalier attendant, general of the left guard, grand herald, and palace attendant, then left the capital as General Who Spreads Might and governor of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 永嘉初，徵為中書監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongjia era he was summoned as Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongjia reign he was recalled to serve as director of the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 于時天下大亂，敦悉以公主時侍婢百餘人配給將士，金銀寶物散之於眾，單車還洛。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was in great chaos; Dun assigned more than a hundred maidservants from the princess's household to the officers and soldiers, scattered gold, silver, and treasures among them, and returned alone in a single carriage to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was coming apart; Wang Dun gave the princess's hundred-odd maids to his troops, distributed her gold and jewels among them, and rode back to Luoyang almost alone.

sentences.zh: 東海王越自滎陽來朝，敦謂所親曰：「今威權悉在太傅，而選用表情，尚書猶以舊制裁之，太傅今至，必有誅罰。

translations.literal: Prince of East China Sima Yue came from Xingyang to court; Dun said to those close to him, "Now all authority lies with the Grand Tutor, yet appointments still go up as memorials and the Masters of Writing check them by old rules; when the Grand Tutor arrives, there will surely be executions and punishments."
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Donghai, Sima Yue, marched in from Xingyang, Wang Dun told his intimates, "Power now sits with the grand tutor, but personnel orders still pass through the Masters of Writing under the old rules. Once Yue is here, heads will roll."

sentences.zh: 」俄而越收中書令繆播等十餘人殺之。

translations.literal: " Soon Yue seized Palace Secretariat Director Mu Bo and more than ten others and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Yue arrested the palace secretariat director Mu Bo and a dozen others and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 越以敦為揚州刺史，潘滔說越曰：「今樹處仲于江外，使其肆豪強之心，是見賊也。

translations.literal: Yue appointed Dun as Governor of Yang Province; Pan Tao advised Yue, saying, "Now planting Chuzhong beyond the Yang is letting him indulge a despot's heart—it is handing arms to a bandit."
translations.idiomatic: Yue named Wang Dun governor of Yang Province. Pan Tao warned him, "Posting Chuzhong south of the river only feeds his arrogance—you are arming your enemy."

sentences.zh: 」越不從。

translations.literal: " Yue did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Yue ignored him.

sentences.zh: 其後徵拜尚書，不就。

translations.literal: Afterwards he was summoned and appointed Master of the Palace, but he did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun was later summoned as master of the palace but declined to serve.

sentences.zh: 元帝召為安東軍諮祭酒。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan summoned him as Libationer for Military Consultation on the Army of Pacification of the East.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Rui, as Prince of Langya, called him in as army libationer for the eastern expedition.

sentences.zh: 會揚州刺史劉陶卒，帝復以敦為揚州刺史，加廣武將軍。

translations.literal: When Governor of Yang Province Liu Tao died, the Emperor again appointed Dun as Governor of Yang Province and added the title General Who Spreads Might.
translations.idiomatic: After Governor Liu Tao of Yang died, the prince again made Wang Dun governor of Yang and confirmed his rank as General Who Spreads Might.

sentences.zh: 尋進左將軍、都督征討諸軍事、假節。

translations.literal: Shortly he was advanced to General of the Left, Area Commander-in-Chief for all campaigning armies, and invested with the staff of authority.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon raised to general of the left, commander of all expeditionary forces, and granted the credential staff.

sentences.zh: 帝初鎮江東，威名未著，敦與從弟導等同心翼戴，以隆中興，時人為之語曰：「王與馬，共天下。

translations.literal: When the Emperor first established his rule east of the Yang, his prestige was not yet renowned; Dun and his cousin Dao and others joined hearts in supporting him to secure the revival; people of the time made a saying of it: "The Wangs and the Ma—together they share the realm."
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Rui first crossed to the lower Yangzi he still lacked prestige; Wang Dun and his cousin Wang Dao carried him on their shoulders, and a rhyme ran through the south: "The Wangs and the Mas split the world between them."

sentences.zh: 」尋與甘卓等討江州刺史華軼，斬之。

translations.literal: " Soon together with Gan Zhuo and others he attacked Governor of Jiang Province Hua Yi and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Gan Zhuo in striking down Hua Yi, governor of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 蜀賊杜弢作亂，荊州刺史周顗退走，敦遣武昌太守陶侃、豫章太守周訪等討韜，而敦進住豫章，為諸軍繼援。

translations.literal: The Shu bandit Du Tao rebelled; Governor of Jing Province Zhou Yi retreated; Dun dispatched Wuchang Administrator Tao Kan, Yuzhang Administrator Zhou Fang, and others to campaign against Du Tao—the manuscript graphs the name as Tao—while Dun advanced to Yuzhang as reinforcement for the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sichuan rebel Du Tao rose, Zhou Yi abandoned Jing Province; Wang Dun sent Tao Kan from Wuchang and Zhou Fang from Yuzhang against him—the target was Du Tao, though the received text uses a homophone graph—and moved his own headquarters to Yuzhang to back the coalition.

sentences.zh: 及侃破弢，敦上侃為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: When Kan defeated Tao, Dun memorialized recommending Kan as Governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Tao Kan broke Du Tao, Wang Dun memorialized to make him governor of Jing.

sentences.zh: 既而侃為弢將杜曾所敗，敦以處分失所，自貶為廣武將軍，帝不許。

translations.literal: Before long Kan was defeated by Tao's general Du Zeng; Dun, holding himself responsible for misdirecting the operation, demoted himself to General Who Spreads Might, but the Emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Kan was soon crushed by Du Tao's lieutenant Du Zeng; Wang Dun blamed his own dispositions, tried to demote himself to General Who Spreads Might, and the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 侃之滅弢也，敦以元帥進鎮東大將軍、開府儀同三司，加都督江揚荊湘交廣六州諸軍事、江州刺史，封漢安侯。

translations.literal: When Kan destroyed Tao, Dun, as supreme commander, was advanced to Grand General Who Guards the East, with office equal to the Three Offices, added Area Commander-in-Chief for the six provinces of Jiang, Yang, Jing, Xiang, Jiao, and Guang, Governor of Jiang Province, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Han'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Tao fell, Wang Dun—as theater commander—became grand general who guards the east with a separate administration matching the three dukes, governor of six provinces from Jiang to Guang, military governor of Jiang, and marquis of Han'an.

sentences.zh: 敦始自選置，兼統州郡焉。

translations.literal: Dun thereupon began appointing his own men and also held commandery and prefecture under unified control.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he picked his own subordinates and treated whole prefectures as his personal fief.

sentences.zh: 頃之，杜弢將杜弘南走廣州，求討桂林賊自效，敦許之。

translations.literal: Before long Du Tao's general Du Hong fled south to Guangzhou seeking to campaign against the Guilin bandits to redeem himself; Dun permitted him.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong, another of Du Tao's officers, fled to Guangzhou offering to redeem himself by crushing bandits in Guilin; Wang Dun assented.

sentences.zh: 陶侃距弘不得進，乃詣零陵太守尹奉降，奉送弘與敦，敦以為將，遂見寵待。

translations.literal: Tao Kan blocked Hong and would not let him advance; Hong therefore went to surrender to Lingling Administrator Yin Feng; Feng sent Hong to Dun, who appointed him a general, whereupon Hong came to be favored.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan barred his path, so Du Hong surrendered to Yin Feng at Lingling, who forwarded him to Wang Dun; Dun took him on as a general and soon showered him with favor.

sentences.zh: 南康人何欽所居險固，聚黨數千人，敦就加四品將軍，於是專擅之跡漸彰矣。

translations.literal: He Qin of Nankang lived in a defensible stronghold and gathered a band of several thousand men; Dun enfeoffed him ad hoc as a fourth-rank general—thus the traces of his monopolizing power gradually became plain.
translations.idiomatic: He Qin of Nankang held mountain fastnesses and several thousand followers; Wang Dun invented a fourth-class generalship for him—another sign that he answered to no one.

sentences.zh: 建武初，又遷征南大將軍，開府如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwu era he was again promoted to Grand General Who Conquers the South, with the same opening of a separate office as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Min's Jianwu era he was promoted to grand general who conquers the south, again with an independent headquarters.

sentences.zh: 中興建，拜侍中、大將軍、江州牧。

translations.literal: At the founding of the Restoration he was appointed Palace Attendant, Grand General, and Governor of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Jin court was proclaimed he became palace attendant, grand general, and governor of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 遣部將硃軌、趙誘伐杜曾，為曾所殺，敦自貶，免侍中，並辭牧不拜。

translations.literal: He sent his subordinate generals Zhu Gui and Zhao You to campaign against Du Zeng; they were killed by Zeng. Dun punished himself, was dismissed from Palace Attendant, and also declined the governorship and would not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: His generals Zhu Gui and Zhao You died fighting Du Zeng; Wang Dun stripped himself of the palace attendant title, tried to refuse the governorship, and would not take the seal.

sentences.zh: 尋加荊州牧，敦上疏曰：

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally given the governorship of Jing Province; Dun submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: The court soon added Jing Province to his portfolio; Wang Dun submitted a long memorial:

sentences.zh: 昔漢祖以神武革命，開建帝業，繼以文帝之賢，纂承洪緒，清虛玄默，擬跡成康。

translations.literal: "Of old Han Gaozu, with divine martial prowess, carried out the revolution and founded the imperial enterprise; succeeding him came Emperor Wen's worthiness, who inherited the great undertaking, clear, empty, and silent in rule, modeled his steps on Cheng and Kang.
translations.idiomatic: "Han Gaozu seized the mandate by force of arms; Emperor Wen inherited a secure throne and ruled in quiet restraint, taking the Zhou kings Cheng and Kang as his models."

sentences.zh: 賈誼歎息，以為天下倒懸，雖言有抑揚，不失事體。

translations.literal: Jia Yi sighed and thought the realm hung upside down; though his words rose and fell in tone, they did not miss the substance of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi lamented that the world was inverted; hyperbolic though he sounded, he described the real danger.

sentences.zh: 今聖朝肇建，漸振宏綱，往段匹磾遣使求效忠節，尚未有勞，便以方州與之。

translations.literal: Now the sage court is newly founded and gradually restores the great principle; formerly Duan Pidi sent envoys offering to demonstrate loyal devotion—he had not yet achieved merit—yet a full province was given him.
translations.idiomatic: Our new court is still gathering its strength, yet Duan Pidi had scarcely proved himself when an entire province was dropped into his lap.

sentences.zh: 今靳明等為國雪恥，欲除大逆，此之志望，皆欲附翼天飛。

translations.literal: Now Jin Ming and others are avenging the state's shame and wish to remove great rebels; in this aspiration they all desire to attach their wings and fly to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Jin Ming now claim to wash away national humiliation and destroy traitors; each wants to ride the imperial favor skyward.

sentences.zh: 雖功大宜報，亦宜有以裁之，當杜漸防萌，慎之在始。

translations.literal: Though great merit should be rewarded, there should also be means to curb it; one ought to stop it at the beginning and guard against it while still a sprout—be careful at the start.
translations.idiomatic: Great deeds deserve reward, but reward needs limits—cut ambition at the root before it sprouts.

sentences.zh: 中間不逞，互生事變，皆非忠義，率以一朝之榮。

translations.literal: In the midst of it the unruly breed one another's plots; none of it is true loyalty and righteousness—all pursue a morning's glory.
translations.idiomatic: In the middle ranks, adventurers stir trouble in the name of loyalty when they only chase a morning's glory.

sentences.zh: 天下漸弊，實由於此。

translations.literal: The realm's gradual decay truly comes from this.
translations.idiomatic: The empire's slow rot begins here.

sentences.zh: 春秋之時，天子微弱，諸侯奢侈，晉文思崇周室，至有求隧之請，襄王讓之以禮，聞義而服，自爾諸侯莫敢越度。

translations.literal: In Spring and Autumn times the Son of Heaven was weak; the feudal lords were extravagant; Jin Wen thought to exalt the Zhou house and went so far as to request a funeral tunnel; King Xiang rebuked him with ritual propriety; he heard the right and submitted; thereafter no feudal lord dared overstep.
translations.idiomatic: Even Duke Wen of Jin, who meant to honor the Zhou king, overreached by asking for royal funeral rites; King Xiang checked him with protocol, and the duke yielded—after that no lord dared step past his rank.

sentences.zh: 臣謂前者賊寇未殄，苟以濟事，朝廷諸所加授，頗多爵位兼重。

translations.literal: I say that formerly, while bandit enemies were not yet extinguished, stopgap measures for the task caused many appointments from the court to combine lofty ranks with heavy authority.
translations.idiomatic: I say that while rebels still roamed, the court handed out fat titles to keep generals quiet.

sentences.zh: 今自臣以下，宜皆除之，且以塞群小矜功之望，夷狄無懨之求。

translations.literal: Now from myself down, they ought all to be removed, so as to block the petty men's hope to boast of merit and the barbarians' insatiable demands.
translations.idiomatic: Those honors should now be stripped away, beginning with me, to silence braggarts and deny the steppe lords a lever for greed.

sentences.zh: 若復遷延，顧望流俗，使奸狡生心，遂相怨謗，指摘朝廷，讒諛蜂起，臣有以知陛下無以正之。

translations.literal: If things are delayed again and one looks askance in deference to vulgar opinion, crafty and cunning hearts will arise, and then mutual recrimination and blame against the court will follow, slander swarming up—I have grounds to know Your Majesty will have no way to set it right.
translations.idiomatic: Delay for fear of gossip, and schemers will turn the court into a battlefield of slander—Your Majesty will lose control.

sentences.zh: 此安危之機，天下之望。

translations.literal: This is the hinge of safety and peril; it is what the realm expects.
translations.idiomatic: The realm's safety hangs on this decision.

sentences.zh: 臣門戶特受榮任，備兼權重，渥恩偏隆，寵過公族。

translations.literal: My clan in particular has received lofty appointments, fully vested with weighty authority, biased in favor by thick grace, favor exceeding the ducal houses.
translations.idiomatic: My own family towers above others in rank, power, and imperial favor—more than any ducal house should bear.

sentences.zh: 行路廝賤猶謂不可，臣獨何心可以安之。

translations.literal: Even passing peddlers and mean men say it cannot be right; how alone could I in my heart find peace?
translations.idiomatic: Peddlers on the road call it obscene; how could I sleep soundly?

sentences.zh: 臣一宗誤陛下，傾覆亦將尋至；

translations.literal: If one branch of my clan misleads Your Majesty, overturning destruction will soon follow as well.
translations.idiomatic: If we mislead you, the Wangs will fall—and soon.

sentences.zh: 雖復灰身剖心，陛下追悔將何所及！

translations.literal: Even if I reduce my body to ashes and cut out my heart, of what use would Your Majesty's regret be!
translations.idiomatic: Burn me alive and it would be too late for regret.

sentences.zh: 伏願諒臣至款，及今際會，小解散之，並授賢俊，少慰有識，各得盡其所懷，則人思競勸矣。

translations.literal: I humbly beg you to pardon my utmost sincerity—seize this moment to dissolve it slightly, grant posts together to the worthy and eminent, somewhat comfort those with understanding, let each fulfill what is in his mind, then people will think eagerly of striving.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to accept this blunt plea: trim our offices now, give talent its chance, and let honest men see a path forward—only then will they strive again.

sentences.zh: 州牧之號，所不敢當，輒送所假侍中貂蟬。

translations.literal: The title of Governor of Province I do not dare accept; I respectfully send back the borrowed Palace Attendant insignia—sable tail and cicada crown.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot keep the title of provincial governor; I return the palace attendant's regalia.

sentences.zh: 又宜並官省職，以塞群小覬覦之望。

translations.literal: Offices should also be merged and posts cut, to block the petty men's covetous hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Merge bureaus and cut posts until the opportunists lose hope.

sentences.zh: 帝優詔不許。

translations.literal: The Emperor issued a gracious edict refusing permission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered with a kind edict and refused.

sentences.zh: 又固辭州牧，聽為刺史。

translations.literal: He again firmly declined Governor of Province; he was permitted to serve only as Inspector (cishi).
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun still refused the grand governor's title; the court let him remain a provincial inspector instead.

sentences.zh: 時劉隗用事，頗疏間王氏，導等甚不平之。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Kui was wielding power and increasingly alienated the Wang clan; Dao and others were deeply resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kui was riding high and driving wedges into the Wang family; Wang Dao and his kin simmered with resentment.

sentences.zh: 敦上疏曰：

translations.literal: Dun submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun fired off another memorial:

sentences.zh: 導昔蒙殊寵，委以事機，虛己求賢，竭誠奉國，遂藉恩私，居輔政之重。

translations.literal: "Dao formerly received extraordinary favor, was entrusted with affairs and opportunity, emptied himself to seek worthy men, devoted full sincerity to serving the state; thus relying on private favor he occupied the weight of chief counselor.
translations.idiomatic: "Wang Dao once enjoyed unique trust, handled the levers of power, humbled himself to recruit talent, and pledged the dynasty his loyalty—so private favor lifted him to chief minister."

sentences.zh: 帝王體遠，事義不同，雖皇極初建，道教方闡，惟新之美，猶有所闕。

translations.literal: The way of emperors looks far; the circumstances of service are not the same. Though the supreme pivot was first founded and the way of instruction is just being opened, even the beauty of renewal still has its lacks.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial perspective spans generations; a founding court cannot be perfect even when the rhetoric is fresh.

sentences.zh: 臣每慷慨於遐遠，愧憤于門宗，是以前後表疏，何嘗不寄言及此。

translations.literal: I have often been stirred with indignation from afar and ashamed on behalf of my clan—therefore in the memorials before and after, how have I not always lodged words touching this?
translations.idiomatic: That is why my earlier papers harped on the same worry—I burn for the honor of our house.

sentences.zh: 陛下未能少垂顧眄，暢臣微懷，雲導頃見疏外，所陳如昨，而其萌已著，其為咎責，豈惟導身而已。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has been unable to grant even a little regard and let my humble thoughts speak freely; they say Dao has lately been treated with cold distance—the points I raised are as yesterday, yet the buds have already shown; as for the blame, how could it fall on Dao's person alone?
translations.idiomatic: You have not spared a glance for my pleas; rumor says Wang Dao is being frozen out. I warned you before the rift showed—if there is fault, it is not his alone.

sentences.zh: 群從所蒙，並過才分。

translations.literal: The whole set of cousins have received favor beyond their abilities.
translations.idiomatic: Every cousin of mine holds a post above his talent.

sentences.zh: 導誠不能自量，陛下亦愛忘其短。

translations.literal: Dao truly cannot measure himself; Your Majesty too in loving him forgets his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao cannot gauge his limits; you, in loving him, overlook his slips.

sentences.zh: 常人近情，恃恩昧進，獨犯龍鱗，迷不自了。

translations.literal: Ordinary men, moved by what is near, rely on favor and blindly advance, alone offending the dragon scales, lost and unaware.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary souls cling to favor, press their luck, and brush the dragon's scales without knowing it.

sentences.zh: 臣竊所自憂慮，未詳所由，惶愧踧躇，情如灰土。

translations.literal: What I privately worry over, I do not fully know the reason; I am anxious, ashamed, and at a loss, my feelings like ashes and dust.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot name every fear; I feel only shame and dust in the mouth.

sentences.zh: 天下事大，盡理實難，導雖凡近，未有穢濁之累；

translations.literal: Great affairs of the realm, fully ordering them is truly hard; Dao, though common and ordinary, has not been stained by filth.
translations.idiomatic: Governing a shattered empire is brutal work; Wang Dao is unremarkable, yet he is not corrupt.

sentences.zh: 既往之勳，疇昔之顧，情好綢繆，足以曆薄俗，明君臣，合德義，同古賢。

translations.literal: Past merit, former regard, affection closely bound, suffice to endure thin custom, clarify lord and minister, unite virtue and right principle—like the worthies of old.
translations.idiomatic: Old service and old friendship should steel him against petty spite and keep ruler and minister in moral alignment, as in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 昔臣親受嘉命，云：「吾與卿及茂弘當管鮑之交。

translations.literal: Formerly I personally received your gracious command, saying, "I with you and Maohong shall have the friendship of Guan and Bao."
translations.idiomatic: You once told me, "You, I, and Maohong shall be Guan Zhong and Bao Shuya to one another."

sentences.zh: 」臣忝外任，漸冉十載，訓誘之誨，日有所忘；

translations.literal: " I disgracefully hold outer appointment, drifting nearly ten years; the teachings that instructed me, day by day something is forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: I have rotted on the frontier ten years; not a day passes that I forget your instruction.

sentences.zh: 至於斯命，銘之於心，竊猶眷眷，謂前恩不得一朝而盡。

translations.literal: As for that mandate, I have engraved it in my heart; I still cling to the thought that the former grace could not vanish in a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: I carved that pledge on my heart; I cannot believe your kindness could evaporate overnight.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下聖哲日新，廣延俊乂，臨之以政，齊之以禮。

translations.literal: I prostrate myself in thought: Your Majesty is sage and wise, daily renewed, broadly gathers the eminent; govern them with policy, align them with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: You are daily wiser, drawing talent from every quarter—govern with law, bind them with ritual.

sentences.zh: 頃者令導內綜機密，出錄尚書，杖節京都，並統六軍，既為刺史，兼居重號，殊非人臣之體。

translations.literal: Recently you ordered Dao to manage secrets within and to take title as Recorder of the Masters of Writing without, to hold the credential staff in the capital and command all six armies—both governor and heavy titles together—this is truly not the form proper to a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Lately you made him master secrets inside the palace, recorder of the Masters of Writing outside, credential-bearer in the capital, and commander of all six armies while he still holds a provincial seat—no subject should wear every sash at once.

sentences.zh: 流俗好評，必有譏謗，宜省錄尚書、杖節及都督。

translations.literal: Vulgar opinion loves to judge; there are bound to be sneers—you should reduce the Recorder of the Masters of Writing, the credential staff, and the area command.
translations.idiomatic: The street will gossip; strip him of the recorder's seal, the staff, and the theater command.

sentences.zh: 且王佐之器，當得宏達遠識、高正明斷、道德優備者，以臣暗識，未見其才。

translations.literal: Moreover the vessel of a king's helper ought to be one broad, far-seeing, upright and decisive in judgment, complete in virtue and the Way; with my dull understanding I have not yet seen such talent in anyone.
translations.idiomatic: A true kingmaker should be magnanimous, farsighted, and morally whole; in my dull sight I have met no such paragon.

sentences.zh: 然於見人，未逾於導；

translations.literal: Yet among those I have seen, no one surpasses Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Among men I know, none outshines Wang Dao.

sentences.zh: 加輔翼積年，實盡心力。

translations.literal: Moreover he has assisted for accumulated years and truly exhausted mind and strength.
translations.idiomatic: He has served you for years and poured out his strength.

sentences.zh: 霸王之主，何嘗不任賢使能，共相終始！

translations.literal: Lords who would be hegemons—when did they ever fail to employ the worthy and use the capable, sharing the whole course together!
translations.idiomatic: Which founder ever spurned a flawed genius who stayed loyal to the end?

sentences.zh: 管仲有三歸反坫之識，子犯有臨河要君之責，蕭何、周勃得罪囹圄，然終為良佐。

translations.literal: Guan Zhong had the reproach of the Triple Returns and the ritual stand for inverted cups; Zifan had the blame of pressing the ruler at the river; Xiao He and Zhou Bo suffered guilt in prison—yet in the end they were good assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Zhong broke sumptuary law; Fan Juan cornered his lord on a riverbank; Xiao He and Zhou Bo rotted in jail—yet all finished as pillars of state.

sentences.zh: 以導之才，何能無失，！

translations.literal: Given Dao's talents, how could he be without fault!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao is human; of course he errs.

sentences.zh: 當令任不過分，役其所長，以功補過，要之將來。

translations.literal: You should have his duty not exceed his portion, employ what he excels at, let merit make up for faults—settle the account in future.
translations.idiomatic: Keep his brief within his gifts, play to his strengths, let later deeds erase earlier slips.

sentences.zh: 導性慎密，尤能忍事，善於斟酌，有文章才義，動靜顧問，起予聖懷，外無過寵，公私得所。

translations.literal: Dao by nature is cautious and secretive, especially able to endure provocation, skilled at weighing matters; he has literary skill and moral sense; in movement and repose he consults with you—he awakens our sage liege. Without excessive favor without or within, public and private each obtains what is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: He is discreet, patient, a careful judge, literate and upright; in council he sharpens your judgment. Balance his honors inside and out, and both throne and minister stay healthy.

sentences.zh: 今皇祚肇建，八表承風；

translations.literal: Now the imperial fortune is first founded and the eight directions receive your wind.
translations.idiomatic: The mandate is young; the world still listens for your tone.

sentences.zh: 聖恩不終，則遐邇失望。

translations.literal: If sage favor does not run its course, then near and far will be disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: If that favor breaks off, every quarter will lose heart.

sentences.zh: 天下荒弊，人心易動；

translations.literal: The realm is waste and worn, human hearts easily stirred.
translations.idiomatic: The land is ruined; moods shift overnight.

sentences.zh: 物聽一移，將致疑惑。

translations.literal: Once rumor shifts, it will bring doubt and confusion.
translations.idiomatic: One whisper can tip the realm into panic.

sentences.zh: 臣非敢苟私親親，惟欲忠於社稷。

translations.literal: I dare not privately favor kin out of partiality—I only wish to be loyal to the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: I do not plead for kin from sentiment—I plead for the dynasty's altars.

sentences.zh: 表至，導封以還敦，敦復遣奏之。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, Dao resealed it and returned it to Dun; Dun sent it back to be presented again.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao sealed the draft and returned it; Wang Dun sent it back to the throne unchanged.

sentences.zh: 初，敦務自矯厲，雅尚清談，口不言財色。

translations.literal: At first Dun made a point of disciplining himself and prized pure conversation, spoke never of wealth or women.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Wang Dun cultivated austerity, traded in Pure Conversation, and affected indifference to money and concubines.

sentences.zh: 既素有重名，又立大功于江左，專任閫外，手控強兵，群從貴顯，威權莫貳，遂欲專制朝廷，有問鼎之心。

translations.literal: As he long possessed great reputation and had won great merit south of the Yang, monopolized command beyond the passes, held strong troops in his hand, and his kinsmen were illustrious, with no rival in awe-inspiring power, he thus wished to monopolize the court and harbored the mind to "ask after the tripods.
translations.idiomatic: Reputation, victories on the left bank, frontier command, crack troops, and a clan in every office left him unrivaled; he began to treat the court as his own and to weigh the tripods of Xia.

sentences.zh: 帝畏而惡之，遂引劉隗、刁協等以為心膂。

translations.literal: The emperor feared and detested him, then brought in Liu Kui, Diao Xie, and others as his heart and backbone.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feared him and built a counterweight with Liu Kui, Diao Xie, and their faction.

sentences.zh: 敦益不能平，於是嫌隙始構矣。

translations.literal: Dun all the more could not reconcile himself, and from this the rift began to form.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun could not stomach the slight; the break opened then.

sentences.zh: 每酒後輒詠魏武帝樂府歌曰：「老驥伏櫪，志在千里。

translations.literal: After drinking he always intoned Emperor Wu of Wei's yuefu song: "The old steed in the stable still aspires to a thousand li."
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, he would chant Cao Cao's ballad: "The aging steed in the stall still dreams of a thousand leagues."

sentences.zh: 烈士暮年，壯心不已。

translations.literal: "The steadfast man in twilight years, his fierce heart does not rest."
translations.idiomatic: "The warrior in winter years never shelves his zeal."

sentences.zh: 」以如意打唾壺為節，壺邊盡缺。

translations.literal: " He beat time on a spittoon with a jade ruyi until its rim was notched all around.
translations.idiomatic: He tapped the rhythm on a spittoon with his jade scepter until the ceramic rim was chipped to pieces.

sentences.zh: 及湘州刺史甘卓遷梁州，敦欲以從事中郎陳頒代卓，帝不從，更以譙王承鎮湘州。

translations.literal: When Governor of Xiang Province Gan Zhuo was transferred to Liang Province, Dun wished to replace Zhuo with his clerk Chen Ban, but the Emperor did not consent; instead Prince of Qiao Sima Cheng was sent to hold Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Zhuo was rotated from Xiang to Liang; Wang Dun wanted his aide Chen Ban to succeed him, but the throne installed Prince Qiao, Sima Cheng, at Changsha instead.

sentences.zh: 敦復上表陳古今忠臣見疑于君，而蒼蠅之人交構其間，欲以感動天子。

translations.literal: Dun again submitted a memorial rehearsing how loyal ministers through history had been suspected by their lords while fly-like slanderers wove intrigue between them, intending thereby to move the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun filed another tract on how good men lose a ruler's trust while petty slanderers buzz between them, hoping to sway the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝愈忌憚之。

translations.literal: The Emperor all the more feared and resented him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's fear and resentment only deepened.

sentences.zh: 俄加敦羽葆鼓吹，增從事中郎、掾屬、舍人各二人。

translations.literal: Soon Dun was additionally given feather-canopy processional music, and two more clerks, aides, and attendants each were added to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon granted him feathered canopy and drum escort, plus two extra staff posts at each rank.

sentences.zh: 帝以劉隗為鎮北將軍，戴若思為征西將軍，悉發揚州奴為兵，外以討胡，實禦敦也。

translations.literal: The Emperor appointed Liu Kui General Who Guards the North and Dai Ruosi General Who Conquers the West, and drafted all the bond servants of Yang Province as soldiers—ostensibly to campaign against the Hu, but in truth to guard against Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi made Liu Kui northern commander and Dai Ruosi western commander, armed every bondservant household in Yang Province, and called it a northern expedition—everyone knew it was aimed at Wang Dun.

sentences.zh: 永昌元年，敦率眾內向，以誅隗為名，上疏曰：

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchang, Dun led his host inward toward the capital under the pretext of executing Liu Kui, and submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchang 1 Wang Dun marched on the capital to "purge" Liu Kui and laid a memorial before the throne:

sentences.zh: 劉隗前在門下，邪佞諂媚，譖毀忠良，疑惑聖聽，遂居權寵，撓亂天機，威福自由，有識杜口。

translations.literal: "Liu Kui, while formerly at the palace gate, was wicked, fawning, and slanderous; he destroyed the loyal and good, confused the sage hearing, then came to wield favor and power, disturbed heaven's dispensation, and wielded blessing and might as he pleased, so that men of insight sealed their lips.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kui flattered his way into power, poisoned the emperor's ear against honest men, then hijacked the machinery of state; anyone with sense learned to stay silent.

sentences.zh: 大起事役，勞擾士庶，外托舉義，內自封植；

translations.literal: He launched vast works and corvées, harassing gentry and commoners; outwardly he claimed righteous purpose, inwardly he built his private domain.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted huge labor projects that tormented the people, masking private empire-building as public duty.

sentences.zh: 奢僭過制，乃以黃散為參軍，晉魏已來，未有此比。

translations.literal: His extravagance exceeded regulations—he even made Gentlemen of the Yellow Gates and Cavalier Attendants into army staff; since Jin and Wei there had been no parallel.
translations.idiomatic: He broke every sumptuary rule, turning palace gentlemen into military aides—a novelty not seen since Wei.

sentences.zh: 傾盡帑藏，以自資奉；

translations.literal: He emptied the treasury to supply himself.
translations.idiomatic: He drained the imperial vaults for his own upkeep.

sentences.zh: 賦役不均，百姓嗟怨；

translations.literal: Taxes and labor service fell unevenly; the hundred surnames groaned in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Levies fell unfairly; commoners cursed his name.

sentences.zh: 免良人奴，自為惠澤。

translations.literal: Freeing good commoners from bondage he styled his own gracious favor.
translations.idiomatic: He recast the manumission of serfs as his own gracious favor.

sentences.zh: 自可使其大田以充倉廩，今便割配，皆充隗軍。

translations.literal: They could have been set to great fields to fill the granaries; instead he carved them out and assigned them all to Kui's army.
translations.idiomatic: Those hands should have tilled state land, yet he drafted every able body into Liu Kui's host.

sentences.zh: 臣前求迎諸將妻息，聖恩聽許，而隗絕之，使三軍之士莫不怨憤。

translations.literal: I formerly begged to welcome the wives and children of the various generals; sage grace granted consent, but Kui blocked it, so that no soldier in the three armies failed to nurse resentment.
translations.idiomatic: I once asked leave to bring our officers' families forward; you agreed, but Liu Kui stopped it, embittering every camp.

sentences.zh: 又徐州流人辛苦經載，家計始立，隗悉驅逼，以實己府。

translations.literal: Moreover the displaced people of Xu Province had toiled for years and only just established households; Kui drove them all off to fill his own bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees from Xu had finally put down roots; Liu Kui uprooted them to pack his own payroll.

sentences.zh: 當陛下踐阼之始，投刺王官，本以非常之慶使豫蒙榮分。

translations.literal: At the time Your Majesty first ascended the throne, they presented their name-slips as court officials, expecting an extraordinary grace that would let them share in honor.
translations.idiomatic: When you first took the throne they registered as officials, hoping for a share in the celebration.

sentences.zh: 而更充征役，復依舊名，普取出客，從來久遠，經涉年載，或死亡滅絕，或自贖得免，或見放遣，或父兄時事身所不及，有所不得，輒罪本主，百姓哀憤，怨聲盈路。

translations.literal: Yet they were instead put to expedition service; again under the old labels he universally seized "guest" dependents—some had been so for many years, some households had died out, some had ransomed free, some had been released, some concerned fathers' and elder brothers' affairs that the person himself never touched; whenever anything was missing he punished the original master—the hundred surnames mourned in rage, and complaint filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he threw them back into the levy rolls, chasing down every hereditary client—no matter who had died, bought freedom, or never belonged to the case—then fined the head of household for any gap; the roads rang with outrage.

sentences.zh: 身欲北渡，以遠朝廷為名，而密知機要，潛行險慝，進人退士，高下任心，奸狡饕餮，未有隗比，雖無忌、宰嚭、弘恭、石顯未足為喻。

translations.literal: Though he himself wished to cross north, taking distance from the court as his excuse, he secretly grasped critical secrets, secretly practiced treachery, advanced and dismissed men at whim—crafty, insatiable, none match Kui; even Wu Qi, Bo Pi, Hong Gong, and Shi Xian are an inadequate comparison.
translations.idiomatic: He talks of retiring north while he hoards secrets and sells offices; for greed and guile no one matches him—not even the famous villains of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 是以遐邇憤慨，群後失望。

translations.literal: Therefore near and far are stirred with indignation; the host of lords is disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: So the realm seethes and the regional lords feel betrayed.

sentences.zh: 臣備位宰輔，與國存亡，誠乏平勃濟時之略，然自忘駑駘，志存社稷，豈忍坐視成敗，以虧聖美。

translations.literal: "I occupy a place among the chief ministers; with the state I stand or fall. Truly I lack the timely stratagem of Chen Ping or Zhou Bo, yet forgetting my sorry nag's pace, my mind rests on the altars—I cannot sit watching success or failure and impair sage excellence."
translations.idiomatic: I am no Chen Ping, but I cannot watch the dynasty stumble while claiming to be its pillar.

sentences.zh: 事不獲已，今輒進軍，同討奸孽，願陛下深垂省察，速斬隗首，則眾望厭服，皇祚復隆。

translations.literal: The affair admits no other course: now I advance the army jointly to punish the wicked spawn; I beg Your Majesty to examine this deeply and swiftly behead Kui—then the multitude's hope will be satisfied and the imperial fortune will rise again.
translations.idiomatic: I am marching to cut out this cancer; behead Liu Kui and every army will stand down.

sentences.zh: 隗首朝懸，諸軍夕退。

translations.literal: Let Kui's head hang at dawn and by evening the hosts will withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: One traitor's head at dawn ends the war by dusk.

sentences.zh: 昔太甲不能遵明湯典，顛覆厥度，幸納伊尹之勳，殷道復昌。

translations.literal: Of old King Taijia could not follow the bright ordinances of Tang and overturned his measure; fortunately he accepted the merit of Yi Yin, and the Yin way flourished again.
translations.idiomatic: Taijia of Shang lost the way until Yi Yin locked him away—then the dynasty recovered.

sentences.zh: 漢武雄略，亦惑江充讒佞邪說，至乃父子相屠，流血丹地，終能克悟，不失大綱。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han was heroically strategic, yet he too was deluded by Jiang Chong's slanderous, wicked talk, until father and son slaughtered each other and blood reddened the ground; in the end he was able to awaken and did not lose the great principle.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wudi listened to Jiang Chong and nearly murdered his heir, yet he woke before the state capsized.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，有逾於此，願陛下深垂三思，諮詢善道，則四海乂安，社稷永固矣。

translations.literal: Today's affair exceeds that; I beg Your Majesty to ponder thrice, consult the good way—then within the four seas there will be peace and the altars forever firm.
translations.idiomatic: Our crisis is worse; think three times, heed honest counsel, and the empire will steady again.

sentences.zh: 又曰：

translations.literal: He also said:
translations.idiomatic: The memorial continued:

sentences.zh: 陛下昔鎮揚州，虛心下士，優賢任能，寬以得眾，故君子盡心，小人畢力。

translations.literal: "When Your Majesty formerly governed Yang Province, you emptied yourself before men of worth, honored the worthy and employed the capable, and by leniency won the multitude—so gentlemen gave their full mind and petty men exhausted their strength.
translations.idiomatic: You once ruled Yangzhou with open doors: the wise came forward, the humble toiled willingly.

sentences.zh: 臣以暗蔽，豫奉徽猷，是以遐邇望風，有識自竭，王業遂隆，惟新克建，四海延頸，咸望太平。

translations.literal: I, in my darkness and obscurity, preliminarily received your fine plan; therefore far and near looked to your wind, men of insight exhausted themselves, the royal enterprise then flourished, the renewal was able to be founded, and within the four seas all stretched their necks, each hoping for great peace.
translations.idiomatic: I shared your vision, watched the realm rally to you, and believed peace was near.

sentences.zh: 自從信隗已來，刑罰不中，街談巷議，皆云如吳之將亡。

translations.literal: Since trusting Liu Kui, punishments have missed the mark; street gossip and lane talk all say it is like Wu on the verge of perishing.
translations.idiomatic: Since Liu Kui took your ear, justice has twisted; people whisper this is Eastern Wu all over again.

sentences.zh: 聞之惶惑，精魂飛散，不覺胸臆摧破，泣血橫流。

translations.literal: Hearing it I am dazed; my essence and soul scatter; unknowingly my breast is torn apart and blood crosses my flow.
translations.idiomatic: Each rumor hits me like a blow to the chest—I could weep blood.

sentences.zh: 陛下當全祖宗之業，存神器之重，察臣前後所啟，奈何棄忽忠言，遂信奸佞，誰不痛心！

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought to preserve the enterprise of the ancestors and keep the weight of the sacred regalia; examine what I have opened before and after—how can you cast aside loyal words and trust wicked flatterers? Who would not ache at heart!
translations.idiomatic: Guard your ancestors' throne and the imperial seals; reread my pleas—how can you spurn loyal counsel for a favorite's whispers? Who would not be heartsick!

sentences.zh: 願出臣表，諮之朝臣，介石之幾，不俟終日，令諸軍早還，不至虛擾。

translations.literal: I beg you to take out my memorial and put it before the courtiers; the moment to stand firm as a rock does not wait a full day—order the armies to return early and not bring empty turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Publish this memorial to the ministers; act today—recall the armies before they ravage the land.

sentences.zh: 敦党吳興人沈充起兵應敦。

translations.literal: Dun's partisan Shen Chong of Wuxing raised troops in answer to Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun's ally Shen Chong of Wuxing rose in his support.

sentences.zh: 敦至蕪湖，又上表罪狀刁協。

translations.literal: When Dun reached Wuhu, he again submitted a memorial listing Diao Xie's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuhu he filed another indictment of Diao Xie.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，下詔曰：「王敦憑恃寵靈，敢肆狂逆，方朕太甲，欲見幽囚。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered and issued an edict saying, "Wang Dun, relying on favor he has received, dares to indulge mad rebellion, compares Us to Taijia, and wishes to see Us imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor exploded: "Wang Dun, drunk on imperial favor, dares liken me to Taijia and plot my house arrest.

sentences.zh: 是可忍也，孰不可忍也！

translations.literal: If this may be endured, what may not be endured!
translations.idiomatic: If I swallow this, nothing is unswallowable!

sentences.zh: 今親率六軍，以誅大逆，有殺敦者，封五千戶侯。

translations.literal: Now We personally lead the six armies to execute the great rebel; whoever kills Dun will be enfeoffed marquis of five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: I will lead the host myself; five thousand households to whoever brings me Wang Dun's head.

sentences.zh: 」召戴若思、劉隗並會京師。

translations.literal: " He summoned Dai Ruosi and Liu Kui both to assemble at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled Dai Ruosi and Liu Kui to the capital.

sentences.zh: 敦兄含時為光祿勳，叛奔於敦。

translations.literal: Dun's elder brother Han at the time was Master of Brilliant Carriages; he rebelled and fled to Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han, Wang Dun's elder brother, held the post of master of brilliant horses; he deserted and ran to the rebel camp.

sentences.zh: 敦至石頭，欲攻劉隗，其將杜弘曰：「劉隗死士眾多，未易可克，不如攻石頭。

translations.literal: When Dun reached Stone City he wished to attack Liu Kui; his general Du Hong said, "Liu Kui has many devoted fighters; he is not easy to overcome—better to attack Stone City."
translations.idiomatic: Outside Jinling Wang Dun meant to strike Liu Kui first; Du Hong said, "Kui's fanatics will bleed us—take Stone Fortress instead."

sentences.zh: 周劄少恩，兵不為用，攻之必敗。

translations.literal: Zhou Zha is short on kindness; his soldiers will not fight for him—attack him and he is sure to be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zha never inspired loyalty; his garrison will not hold.

sentences.zh: 劄敗，則隗自走。

translations.literal: If Zha is defeated, Kui will flee of himself.
translations.idiomatic: Crack the fortress and Liu Kui runs.

sentences.zh: 」敦從之。

translations.literal: " Dun followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun took the advice.

sentences.zh: 劄果開城門納弘。

translations.literal: Zha indeed opened the city gate and admitted Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zha opened the gates and let Du Hong in.

sentences.zh: 諸將與敦戰，王師敗績。

translations.literal: The various generals fought Dun; the royal army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial troops met him in battle and broke.

sentences.zh: 既入石頭，擁兵不朝，放肆兵士劫掠內外。

translations.literal: Once inside Stone City he held his troops and did not attend court, letting his soldiers plunder inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: He occupied the fortress, skipped audience, and turned his men loose to loot.

sentences.zh: 官省奔散，惟有侍中二人侍帝。

translations.literal: The palace bureaus fled in disorder; only two palace attendants remained attending the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries fled; two attendants alone stayed with the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 帝脫戎衣，著朝服，顧而言曰：「欲得我處，但當早道，我自還琅邪，何至困百姓如此！

translations.literal: The Emperor took off military garb, put on court dress, looked about and said, "If you wanted my place, you had only to say so early—I would have returned to Langya myself; why bring the hundred surnames to such distress!"
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi shed his armor for court robes and said, "Had you asked for the throne plainly, I would have gone back to Langya—why torture the people?"

sentences.zh: 」敦收周顗、戴若思害之。

translations.literal: " Dun seized Zhou Yi and Dai Ruosi and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: He then seized Zhou Yi and Dai Ruosi and executed them.

sentences.zh: 以敦為丞相、江州牧，進爵武昌郡公，邑萬戶，使太常荀崧就拜，又加羽葆鼓吹，並偽讓不受。

translations.literal: Dun was appointed Chancellor and Governor of Jiang Province, advanced in noble rank to Duke of Wuchang commandery with a fief of ten thousand households; Minister of Ceremonies Xun Song was sent to invest him; feather-canopy processional music was again added, and he feigned refusal and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him chancellor and governor of Jiang, duke of Wuchang with ten thousand households; Xun Song brought the patent and regalia, and Wang Dun theatrically declined.

sentences.zh: 還屯武昌，多害忠良，寵樹親戚，以兄含為衛將軍、都督沔南軍事、領南蠻校尉、荊州刺史，以義陽太守任愔督河北諸軍事、南中郎將，敦又自督寧、益二州。

translations.literal: He returned to garrison Wuchang, killed many loyal and good men, lavishly planted his kin: he made his elder brother Han General Who Guards the Palace, area commander of the south of the Han River, chief of the southern Man, Governor of Jing Province; made Yiyang Administrator Ren Yin area commander of the north of the He, General of the Center of the South; Dun himself additionally commanded Ning and Yi provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to Wuchang, purged loyalists, and packed offices with Wangs: Wang Han guarded the Han basin; Ren Yin held the Yellow River line; Wang Dun added Ning and Yi to his portfolio.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，太甯元年，敦諷朝廷徵己，明帝乃手詔徵之，語在《明帝紀》。

translations.literal: When the Emperor died, in the first year of Taining, Dun hinted that the court should summon him; Emperor Ming then personally drafted an edict summoning him—the wording is recorded in the *Annals of Emperor Ming*.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan's death, in Taining 1 Wang Dun hinted for a recall; Emperor Ming's handwritten summons is recorded in the *Annals of Emperor Ming*.

sentences.zh: 又使兼太常應詹拜授加黃龯，班劍武賁二十人，奏事不名，入朝不趨，劍覆上殿。

translations.literal: He also had concurrent Minister of Ceremonies Ying Zhan go to invest him, adding the yellow battle-axe, twenty guards with patterned swords, permission to memorialize without giving name, to enter court without hurrying, and to wear sword and shoes on the dais.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Ying Zhan with the yellow axe, twenty household guards, privilege to report without name, to walk the hall without trotting, and to bear sword and shoes before the throne.

sentences.zh: 敦移鎮姑孰，帝使侍中阮孚齎牛酒犒勞，敦稱疾不見，使主簿受詔。

translations.literal: Dun moved his headquarters to Gushu; the Emperor sent Palace Attendant Ruan Fu to bring cattle and wine as consolation; Dun claimed illness and would not meet him, having his chief clerk receive the edict.
translations.idiomatic: He shifted to Gushu; Ruan Fu arrived with imperial wine and cattle, but Wang Dun pleaded illness and made his registrar take the edict.

sentences.zh: 以王導為司徒，敦自為揚州牧。

translations.literal: Wang Dao was made Minister of Education; Dun himself became Governor of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao became minister of education while Wang Dun seized Yang Province for himself.

sentences.zh: 敦既得志，暴慢愈甚，四方貢獻多入己府，將相嶽牧悉出其門。

translations.literal: Once Dun had realized his aims, his violence and arrogance grew worse; regional tribute mostly entered his own storehouse; generals, ministers, mountain and pasture officials all issued from his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Victory made him worse: tribute flowed to his private treasury, every generalship a Wang appointment.

sentences.zh: 徙含為征東將軍、都督揚州江西諸軍事，從弟舒為荊州，彬為江州，邃為徐州。

translations.literal: Han was transferred to General Who Conquers the East, area commander of military affairs west of the Yang in Yang Province; cousins Shu held Jing, Bin held Jiang, and Sui held Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han took the lower Yangzi theater; Wang Shu, Wang Bin, and Wang Sui held Jing, Jiang, and Xu.

sentences.zh: 含字處弘，凶頑剛暴，時所不齒，以敦貴重，故曆顯位。

translations.literal: Han, styled Chuhong, was fierce, obstinate, and violent; the age despised him, but because Dun was powerful and honored he repeatedly held eminent posts.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han was a brute the world despised; his brother's clout kept him in high office.

sentences.zh: 敦以沈充、錢鳳為謀主，諸葛瑤、鄧岳、周撫、李恆、謝雍為爪牙。

translations.literal: Dun made Shen Chong and Qian Feng his chief plotters, Zhuge Yao, Deng Yue, Zhou Fu, Li Heng, and Xie Yong his claws and fangs.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chong and Qian Feng planned for him; Zhuge Yao, Deng Yue, Zhou Fu, Li Heng, and Xie Yong did the dirty work.

sentences.zh: 充等並凶險驕恣，共相驅扇，殺戮自己；

translations.literal: Chong and the rest were alike cruel, dangerous, and arrogant, urging one another on, killing and slaughtering at will;
translations.idiomatic: They were a pack of swaggering killers who stirred one another on;

sentences.zh: 又大起營府，侵人田宅，發掘古墓，剽掠市道，士庶解體，咸知其禍敗焉。

translations.literal: they also raised great camp offices, encroached on others' fields and houses, dug open ancient tombs, and plundered the markets and roads—gentry and commoners fell apart, all knowing disaster and ruin were coming.
translations.idiomatic: they built sprawling headquarters, seized farmland, looted tombs, and robbed markets until everyone saw the crash coming.

sentences.zh: 敦從弟豫章太守棱日夜切諫，敦怒，陰殺之。

translations.literal: Dun's cousin Wang Ling, Administrator of Yuzhang, remonstrated urgently day and night; Dun, angry, secretly killed him.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Wang Ling, governor of Yuzhang, argued with him nightly; Wang Dun had him murdered quietly.

sentences.zh: 敦無子，養含子應。

translations.literal: Dun had no sons; he adopted Han's son Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, he adopted Wang Han's son Wang Ying.

sentences.zh: 及敦病甚，拜應為武衛將軍以自副。

translations.literal: When Dun was gravely ill, he appointed Ying General Who Guards Martiality as his own deputy.
translations.idiomatic: As he sickened he named Wang Ying guard general as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 錢鳳謂敦曰：「脫其不諱，便當以後事付應。

translations.literal: Qian Feng said to Dun, "If the worst should happen, you ought to entrust the aftermath to Ying."
translations.idiomatic: Qian Feng whispered, "When you die, hand power to Wang Ying."

sentences.zh: 」敦曰：「非常之事，豈常人所能！

translations.literal: Dun said, "An extraordinary deed is not something ordinary men can manage!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun answered, "Only extraordinary men handle extraordinary crises!"

sentences.zh: 且應年少，安可當大事。

translations.literal: "Moreover Ying is young—how could he shoulder great affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: "The boy is too young for that burden."

sentences.zh: 我死之後，莫若解眾放兵，歸身朝廷，保全門戶，此計之上也。

translations.literal: "After my death, better to disband the host, release the troops, return yourself to the court, and preserve the gate and door—that is the upper plan."
translations.idiomatic: "After I die, disarm, submit to the throne, and save the clan—that is the best course."

sentences.zh: 退還武昌，收兵自守，貢獻不廢，亦中計也。

translations.literal: "Fall back to Wuchang, gather troops and guard yourself, keep tribute unceased—that too is a middling plan."
translations.idiomatic: "Retreat to Wuchang, dig in, keep sending tribute—that is the middling course."

sentences.zh: 及吾尚存，悉眾而下，萬一僥倖，計之下也。

translations.literal: "While I still live, lead the full host downstream—if by chance you succeed, that is the lowest plan."
translations.idiomatic: "Or strike now with every man while I breathe—that is a desperate gamble."

sentences.zh: 」鳳謂其黨曰：「公之下計，乃上策也。

translations.literal: Feng said to his clique, "The lord's lowest plan is the upper strategy."
translations.idiomatic: Qian Feng told his circle, "His worst idea is actually our best."

sentences.zh: 」遂與沈充定謀，須敦死後作難。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he and Shen Chong settled a plot to raise trouble after Dun died.
translations.idiomatic: He and Shen Chong planned a coup for the moment Wang Dun died.

sentences.zh: 敦又忌周劄，殺之而盡滅其族。

translations.literal: Dun also envied Zhou Zha; he killed him and exterminated his whole clan.
translations.idiomatic: He also envied Zhou Zha, killed him, and wiped out his family.

sentences.zh: 常從督冉曾、公乘雄等為元帝腹心，敦又害之。

translations.literal: Routine adjutants Ran Zeng and Gongsheng Xiong had been trusted intimates of Emperor Yuan; Dun killed them as well.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Zeng and Gongsheng Xiong, Ming's old confidants, died on his orders too.

sentences.zh: 以宿衛尚多，奏令三番休二。

translations.literal: Because the palace guard was still numerous, he memorialized ordering three shifts to rest two.
translations.idiomatic: Too many guards remained at the palace, so he had rotations thinned to two-thirds strength.

sentences.zh: 及敦病篤，詔遣侍中陳晷、散騎常侍虞問疾。

translations.literal: When Dun's illness was critical, an edict sent Palace Attendant Chen Jiu and Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Yu to inquire after his illness.
translations.idiomatic: As he lay dying the court sent Chen Jiu and Yu to ask after his health.

sentences.zh: 時帝將討敦，微服至蕪湖，察其營壘，又屢遣大臣訊問其起居。

translations.literal: At the time the Emperor was about to campaign against Dun; in disguise he reached Wuhu and inspected his ramparts, and repeatedly sent great ministers to ask after his daily condition.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming, preparing war, slipped to Wuhu in plain clothes to scout his works and sent ministers to pry on his condition.

sentences.zh: 遷含驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，含子瑜散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Han was promoted to Grand General of Agile Cavalry with office equal to the Three Offices; Han's son Yu was made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han became grand general of agile cavalry with a separate administration; his son Wang Yu entered the palace corps.

sentences.zh: 敦以溫嶠為丹陽尹，欲使覘伺朝廷。

translations.literal: Dun made Wen Jiao Administrator of Danyang, intending to have him spy on the court.
translations.idiomatic: He named Wen Jiao governor of Danyang to spy on Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 嶠至，具言敦逆謀。

translations.literal: When Jiao arrived, he fully reported Dun's rebellious plot.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Jiao reached the capital and exposed the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 帝欲討之，知其為物情所畏服，乃偽言敦死，於是下詔曰：

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to punish him; knowing men feared and submitted to Dun, he falsely announced that Dun had died, then issued an edict saying:
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi meant to strike but knew the realm still feared Wang Dun, so he spread word that Wang Dun was dead and published an edict:

sentences.zh: 先帝以聖德應運，創業江東，司徒導首居心膂，以道翼讚。

translations.literal: "The late Emperor, with sage virtue answering to the mandate, founded the enterprise east of the Yang; Minister of Education Dao was first among heart and backbone, assisting with the Way.
translations.idiomatic: The late sovereign built the eastern court; Wang Dao was his right hand.

sentences.zh: 故大將軍敦參處股肱，或內或外，夾輔之勳，與有力焉。

translations.literal: Therefore the Grand General Dun participated as thigh and arm; whether within or without, in the merit of supporting him on both sides he had a share of strength.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun served as his strong arm, within and without.

sentences.zh: 階緣際會，遂據上宰，杖節專征，委以五州。

translations.literal: By steps of opportunity he then occupied the highest minister, grasped the staff with sole command, and was entrusted with five provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Chance raised him to chief minister, credential in hand, over five provinces.

sentences.zh: 刁協、劉隗立朝不允，敦抗義致討，情希鬻拳，兵雖犯順，猶嘉乃誠，禮秩優崇，人臣無貳。

translations.literal: Diao Xie and Liu Kui stood at court without fairness; Dun raised righteous arms to chastise them—his feeling hoped to match Yu Quan's remonstrance; though the troops offended against obedience, We still honored his sincerity, kept his rites and rank generous—no second subject matched him.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Xie and Liu Kui skewed justice; Wang Dun marched to "correct" them—like Yu Quan who maimed himself to warn his king. The march was treason, yet the late emperor indulged him.

sentences.zh: 事解之後，劫掠城邑，放恣兵人，侵及宮省；

translations.literal: After the affair was resolved he plundered cities, let his troops run wild, and encroached on palace and ministries;
translations.idiomatic: Peace brought only looting and soldiers in the palace.

sentences.zh: 背違赦信，誅戮大臣；

translations.literal: he betrayed the amnesty and trust, executed great ministers;
translations.idiomatic: He broke pardons and murdered ministers.

sentences.zh: 縱凶極逆，不朝而退。

translations.literal: he indulged extremity and rebellion, did not attend court, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He shunned audience and marched away.

sentences.zh: 六合阻心，人情同憤。

translations.literal: The six directions were blocked in heart; human feeling shared indignation.
translations.idiomatic: The world turned against him.

sentences.zh: 先帝含垢忍恥，容而不責，委任如舊，禮秩有加。

translations.literal: The late Emperor bore shame and endured insult, tolerated him without blame, entrusted him as before, and increased his rites and rank.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor swallowed the insult and left him in power.

sentences.zh: 朕以不天，尋丁酷罰，煢煢在疚，哀悼靡寄。

translations.literal: We, lacking heaven's favor, soon suffered harsh bereavement; alone in grief, We have nowhere to lodge mourning.
translations.idiomatic: I am young, orphaned, drowning in grief.

sentences.zh: 而敦曾無臣子追遠之誠，又無輔孤同獎之操，繕甲聚兵，盛夏來至，輒以天官假授私屬，將以威脅朝廷，傾危宗社。

translations.literal: Yet Dun never showed the good faith of a subject mindful of what is distant, nor the duty of aiding the orphan in common endeavor; he repaired armor, gathered troops, came in the height of summer, and casually invested private followers with celestial offices, intending to threaten the court and overturn the ancestral altars.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun shows no loyalty to my father's memory nor care for a boy emperor; he arms in summer and sells offices to kin, aiming at the throne.

sentences.zh: 朕湣其狂戾，冀其覺悟，故且含隱以觀其終。

translations.literal: We pity his mad perversity and hoped he might awaken; therefore We temporarily concealed matters to watch the outcome.
translations.idiomatic: I humored his madness hoping he would wake.

sentences.zh: 而敦矜其不義之強，有侮弱朝廷之志，棄親用羈，背賢任惡。

translations.literal: Yet Dun boasts of his illegitimate might, harbors a mind to bully the weak court, casts aside kin and employs outsiders, turns from the worthy and trusts the wicked.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he struts, bullies a child throne, favors strangers over kin, trusts villains.

sentences.zh: 錢鳳豎子，專為謀主，逞其凶慝，誣罔忠良。

translations.literal: Qian Feng is a petty fellow, solely his plot chief, displaying his fierce wickedness, slandering the loyal and good.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Feng, a guttersnipe, plots for him and frames good men.

sentences.zh: 周嵩亮直，讜言致禍；

translations.literal: Zhou Song was bright and straight; forthright words brought disaster;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Song died for speaking truth;

sentences.zh: 周劄、周莚累世忠義，聽受讒構，殘夷其宗。

translations.literal: Zhou Zha and Zhou Yan, generations of loyalty and righteousness, listened to slanderous fabrications and had their clans mutilated and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zha and Zhou Yan served faithfully yet were exterminated on gossip.

sentences.zh: 秦人之酷，刑不過五。

translations.literal: The cruelty of the Qin state did not exceed five punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Even Qin law stopped at five punishments.

sentences.zh: 敦之誅戮，傍濫無辜，滅人之族，莫知其罪。

translations.literal: Dun's executions and slaughters spread sideways to the innocent; clans were extinguished without knowing their crime.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun kills without charge and wipes out whole houses.

sentences.zh: 天下駭心，道路以目。

translations.literal: Within the realm hearts were appalled; on the roads people dared only signal with their eyes.
translations.idiomatic: The empire went silent with fear—on the highway people traded warnings with a glance.

sentences.zh: 神怒人怨，篤疾所嬰，昏荒悖逆，日以滋其，輒立兄息以自承代，多樹私黨，莫非同惡，未有宰相繼體而不由王命者也。

translations.literal: Spirits angry and men resentful, gripped by grave illness, benighted, wild, and rebellious, day by day it grew worse; he thereupon set up his elder brother's son to succeed himself in his place, planted many private factions, none not sharing the same wickedness—never has a chief minister's heir succeeded without a kingly mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and the people turned against him: sick, muddled, and daily more outrageous, he tried to install his nephew as heir and pack the court with cronies—no legitimate succession behaves that way.

sentences.zh: 頑凶相獎，無所顧忌，擅錄冶工，輒割運漕，志騁凶醜，以窺神器。

translations.literal: The stubborn and vicious encouraged one another, without anything they feared or forbore; he seized foundry workers at will, cut off transport grain—his will galloped through foul crime as he spied on the sacred regalia.
translations.idiomatic: They egged each other on, seized smiths, hijacked river grain, and angled for the throne itself.

sentences.zh: 社稷之危，匪夕則旦。

translations.literal: The altars' peril was not evening but dawn.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty had hours, not years, left.

sentences.zh: 天下長奸，敦以隕斃。

translations.literal: The realm long nursed treachery; Dun has met death and fallen.
translations.idiomatic: The world had learned villainy from Wang Dun—now he is dead.

sentences.zh: 鳳承凶宄，彌復煽逆。

translations.literal: Feng inherited the vicious remnant and all the more fanned rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Feng carried his master's malice forward and stoked revolt.

sentences.zh: 是可忍也，孰不可忍也！

translations.literal: If this may be endured, what may not be endured!
translations.idiomatic: If we tolerate this, nothing is intolerable!

sentences.zh: 今遣司徒導，鎮南將軍、丹陽尹嶠，建威將軍趙胤武旅三萬，十道並進；

translations.literal: Now We send Minister of Education Dao, General Who Guards the South and Danyang Governor Qiao, and General Who Establishes Might Zhao Yin with thirty thousand picked troops advancing along ten routes at once.
translations.idiomatic: I dispatch Wang Dao, Wen Jiao, and Zhao Yin with thirty thousand veterans on ten columns.

sentences.zh: 平西將軍邃率兗州刺史遐、奮武將軍峻、奮威將軍贍精銳三萬，水陸齊勢；

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West Sui leads Yan Governor Xia, General Who Rouses Might Jun, and General Who Rouses Glory Shan with thirty thousand elite, matching land and water power.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sui brings Liu Xia, Zu Jun, and another column—another thirty thousand by land and river.

sentences.zh: 朕親禦六軍，左衛將軍亮，右衛將軍胤，護軍將軍詹，領軍將軍瞻，中軍將軍壺，驍騎將軍艾，驃騎將軍、南頓王宗，鎮軍將軍、汝南王祐，太宰、西陽王羕被練三千，組甲三萬，總統諸軍，討鳳之罪。

translations.literal: We personally command the six armies: Generals of the Left and Right Guards Liang and Yin, Protector General Zhan, Army Inspector General Zhan, Central Army General Hu, Swift Cavalry General Ai, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Prince of Nandun, Zong, General Who Guards the Army, Prince of Runan, You, Grand Preceptor, Prince of Xiyang, Yang—with three thousand silk-armored troops and thirty thousand linked-armor soldiers, overall commanding the hosts to punish Feng's crime.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor leads the household guards: Yu Liang, Zhao Yin, Ying Zhan, the princes of Nandun, Runan, and Xiyang, Bian Hu, and more—thousands in white silk armor and tens of thousands in lamellar mail—all aimed at Qian Feng.

sentences.zh: 罪止一人，朕不濫刑。

translations.literal: Guilt stops at one man; We will not punish indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: Only the ringleader pays; there will be no blanket purge.

sentences.zh: 有能殺鳳送首，封五千戶侯，賞布五千匹。

translations.literal: Whoever can kill Feng and deliver his head will be enfeoffed marquis of five thousand households and rewarded with five thousand bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand households and five thousand bolts to whoever brings Qian Feng's head.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍鄧岳志氣平厚，識經邪正；

translations.literal: General Who Takes the Crown Deng Yue is steady in temper, broad in mind, and discriminates crooked from straight.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yue is calm, seasoned, and knows right from wrong.

sentences.zh: 前將軍周撫質性詳簡，義誠素著；

translations.literal: General of the Front Zhou Fu is plain and careful in nature, and loyal integrity has long been plain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fu is sober, steady, and proven loyal.

sentences.zh: 功臣之胄，情義兼常，往年從敦，情節不展，畏逼首領，不得相違，論其乃心，無貳王室，朕嘉其誠，方任之以事。

translations.literal: As scions of merit-makers, their affection and duty are more than ordinary; in years past they followed Dun, their true intent could not unfold, threatened in life they could not disobey—judging their inner heart, they have no second loyalty to the royal house; We praise their sincerity and will entrust them with affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They marched with Wang Dun under duress; their hearts never left the throne—I mean to use them in earnest.

sentences.zh: 其餘文武，諸為敦所授用者，一無所問，刺史二千石不得輒離所職。

translations.literal: The rest of civil and military, all whom Dun appointed, are questioned on nothing; governors and two-thousand-bushel officials may not leave their posts without order.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone else keeps his post; no prefect may bolt without leave.

sentences.zh: 書到奉承，自求多福，無或猜嫌，以取誅滅。

translations.literal: When the letter arrives, obey it and seek your own blessing; do not breed suspicion and invite execution and extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Read this edict, choose wisely, and do not invite annihilation.

sentences.zh: 敦之將士，從敦彌所，怨曠日久，或父母隕沒，或妻子喪亡，不得奔赴，銜哀從役，朕甚湣之，希不悽愴。

translations.literal: Dun's officers and soldiers, wherever they followed Dun, have long suffered separation and longing; some had parents die, some wives and children perish, yet could not hurry to mourning, bearing grief while under orders—We pity them greatly and hope they are not overwhelmed.
translations.idiomatic: The men who served Wang Dun have buried parents and wives from afar—I pity their grief.

sentences.zh: 其單丁在軍無有兼重者，皆遣歸家，終身不調，其餘皆與假三年，休訖還台，當與宿衛同例三番。

translations.literal: Those sole sons in the army without double burdens are all sent home and never drafted again; the rest are all granted three years' leave, and when rest ends they return to the terrace and will serve in palace guard rotation like the old three-on, two-off rule.
translations.idiomatic: Only sons go home for good; everyone else gets three years off, then returns to the capital rotation.

sentences.zh: 明承詔書，朕不負信。

translations.literal: Understand this edict clearly: We do not break faith.
translations.idiomatic: Mark my word: the throne keeps its promises.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「敢有舍王敦姓名而稱大將軍者，軍法從事。」

translations.literal: Another edict said, "Whoever dares omit Wang Dun's name and only call him Grand General will be dealt with by military law."
translations.idiomatic: A follow-up edict threatened death for anyone who called him merely "Grand General" instead of naming Wang Dun.

sentences.zh: 敦病轉篤，不能禦眾，使錢鳳、鄧岳、周撫等率眾三萬向京師。

translations.literal: Dun's illness turned more critical; he could not command the host, so he had Qian Feng, Deng Yue, Zhou Fu, and others lead thirty thousand toward the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Too sick to lead, Wang Dun ordered Qian Feng, Deng Yue, and Zhou Fu toward Jiankang with thirty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 含謂敦曰：「此家事，吾便當行。

translations.literal: Han said to Dun, "This is a family matter; I myself shall go."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han told him, "This is our clan's fight—I will command."

sentences.zh: 」於是以含為元帥。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Han was made supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han took supreme command.

sentences.zh: 鳳等問敦曰：「事克之日，天子云何？

translations.literal: Feng and the others asked Dun, "On the day the affair succeeds, what of the Son of Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Qian Feng asked what to do with the emperor after victory?

sentences.zh: 」敦曰：「尚未南郊，何得稱天子！

translations.literal: Dun said, "He has not yet sacrificed at the southern suburb—how can he be called Son of Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun sneered, "He has never offered the suburban sacrifice—how can you call him Son of Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 便盡卿兵勢，保護東海王及裴妃而已。

translations.literal: Exhaust your military might to protect the Prince of East China and Consort Pei, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Throw your whole force around Prince Donghai and his consort—nothing more.

sentences.zh: 」乃上疏罪狀溫嶠，以誅奸臣為名。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he submitted a memorial listing Wen Jiao's crimes, under the name of executing wicked ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized against Wen Jiao, again cloaking treason as "purging traitors."

sentences.zh: 含至江甯，司徒導遺含書曰：

translations.literal: When Han reached Jiangning, Minister of Education Dao sent Han a letter saying:
translations.idiomatic: Near Nanjing Wang Dao wrote Wang Han:

sentences.zh: 近承大將軍困篤綿綿，或云已有不諱，悲怛之情，不能自勝。

translations.literal: "Lately I have received word that the Grand General's illness drags on; some say the worst has already come—I cannot master my grief and pain.
translations.idiomatic: They say Wang Dun is dying—my heart breaks.

sentences.zh: 尋知錢鳳大嚴，欲肆奸逆，朝士忿憤，莫不扼腕。

translations.literal: Soon I learned Qian Feng had tightened readiness and meant to indulge treason; courtiers are furious, none not wringing wrists.
translations.idiomatic: Then word came that Qian Feng was mobilizing for revolt—the capital boils.

sentences.zh: 去月二十三日，得征北告，劉遐、陶瞻、蘇峻等深懷憂慮，不謀同辭。

translations.literal: On the twenty-third of last month I received the General Who Conquers the North's report: Liu Xia, Tao Zhan, Su Jun, and others are deeply anxious and, without prior plan, spoke with one voice.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xia, Tao Zhan, and Su Jun all report the same dread.

sentences.zh: 都邑大小及二宮宿衛咸懼有往年之掠，不復保其妻孥，是以聖主發赫斯之命，具如檄旨。

translations.literal: Capital and palace guards alike fear a repeat of last year's plunder and can no longer protect wives and children—therefore the sage lord issued an awe-striking command, fully as the proclamation states.
translations.idiomatic: The city fears another sack; the sovereign issued the orders you have seen.

sentences.zh: 近有嘉詔，崇兄八命，望兄獎群賢忠義之心，抑奸細不逞之計，當還武昌，盡力籓任。

translations.literal: Lately there was a gracious edict elevating you, elder brother, to the eightfold mandate; I hope you will encourage the loyal hearts of the worthy crowd and check the restless schemes of traitorous petty men—you should return to Wuchang and devote yourself to your frontier charge.
translations.idiomatic: The court just honored you, brother—turn back to Wuchang and serve the frontier as you should.

sentences.zh: 卒奉來告，乃承與犬羊俱下，雖當逼近，猶以罔然。

translations.literal: At last your letter arrived, yet it said you were coming downstream with dogs and sheep—though you draw near, I am still at a loss.
translations.idiomatic: Your note says you march with rabble at your heels—even now I cannot believe it.

sentences.zh: 兄立身率素，見信明于門宗，年逾耳順，位極人臣，仲玉、安期亦不足作佳少年，本來門戶，良可惜也！

translations.literal: Elder brother has conducted yourself plainly and been trusted within the clan; you have passed sixty and reached the summit of subject rank—Zhongyu and Anqi are hardly still fine youths; for the gate and door it is truly pitiable!
translations.idiomatic: You are past sixty, honored as no other Wang—yet you drag your sons into this? What a waste of the family name!

sentences.zh: 兄之此舉，謂可得如大將軍昔年之事乎？

translations.literal: Does elder brother suppose this action can match what the Grand General did in former years?
translations.idiomatic: Do you imagine a second march like Wang Dun's first?

sentences.zh: 昔年佞臣亂朝，人懷不寧，如導之徒，心思外濟。

translations.literal: In those years wicked ministers threw the court into chaos and every man felt unsafe; men like Dao thought of rescue from without.
translations.idiomatic: Back then the court was rotten and we looked for help from outside.

sentences.zh: 今則不然。

translations.literal: Now it is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Today is different.

sentences.zh: 大將軍來屯于湖，漸失人心，君子危怖，百姓勞弊。

translations.literal: When the Grand General camped at Yuhu he gradually lost popular support; gentlemen were in peril and fear, the hundred surnames toiled and worn.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun sat at Yuhu he forfeited the people—officials panicked, commoners broke.

sentences.zh: 將終之日，委重安期，安期斷乳未幾日，又乏時望，便可襲宰相之跡邪？
