translations.literal: On the day he was dying he entrusted weight to Anqi; Anqi had been weaned only a few days and moreover lacks timely reputation—can one then usurp a chief minister's footsteps?
translations.idiomatic: He tried to hand power to Wang Ying still wet behind the ears—can an infant play prime minister?

sentences.zh: 自開闢以來，頗有宰相孺子者不？

translations.literal: Since the opening of the age, has there been much of a chief minister who was a suckling child?
translations.idiomatic: Name one regent-in-diapers in all history?

sentences.zh: 諸有耳者皆是將禪代意，非人臣之事也。

translations.literal: Everyone with ears takes it as intention to yield the throne by ritual—it is not the business of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Whispers already call it a usurpation—no subject should do this.

sentences.zh: 先帝中興，遺愛在人。

translations.literal: The late Emperor revived the enterprise; his gracious memory remains among the people.
translations.idiomatic: The late sovereign restored Jin; the people still love his memory.

sentences.zh: 聖主聰明，德洽朝野，思與賢哲弘濟艱難。

translations.literal: The sage lord is discerning; his virtue harmonizes court and countryside; he wishes with the worthy and wise broadly to aid this hardship.
translations.idiomatic: The young emperor is sharp and loved; he wants good men to steady the crisis.

sentences.zh: 不北面而執臣節，乃私相樹建，肆行威福，凡在人臣，誰不憤歎！

translations.literal: Not to turn north and hold subject ritual, yet privately to set up power, wantonly wield blessing and might—among all who are subjects, who fails to rage and sigh!
translations.idiomatic: Yet you refuse fealty and build a private regime—every honest official seethes!

sentences.zh: 此直錢鳳不良之心聞於遠近，自知無地，遂唱奸逆。

translations.literal: This is simply Qian Feng's evil heart heard far and near; knowing he has no ground, he then sings treason.
translations.idiomatic: This is Qian Feng's plot: cornered, he preaches rebellion.

sentences.zh: 至如鄧伯山、周道和恆有好情，往來人士咸皆明之，方欲委任，與共戮力，非徒無慮而已也。

translations.literal: As for Deng Boshan and Zhou Daohe, they have always had good feeling; travelers coming and going all understand it; We were just about to entrust them and join strength together—not merely without worry.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Deng Yue and Zhou Fu remain loyal; the court was about to trust them, not suspect them.

sentences.zh: 導門戶小大受國厚恩，兄弟顯寵，可謂隆矣。

translations.literal: Dao's gate, great and small, has received the state's thick grace; brothers hold brilliant favor—one may call it lofty.
translations.idiomatic: Our Wang house owes the dynasty everything; our rank could not be higher.

sentences.zh: 導雖不武，情在甯國。

translations.literal: Dao, though not a military man, keeps his mind on securing the state.
translations.idiomatic: I am no soldier, but I mean to save the realm.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，明目張膽為六軍之首，甯忠臣而死，不無賴而生矣。

translations.literal: In today's affair I openly stand at the head of the six armies; I would rather die a loyal minister than live a rogue.
translations.idiomatic: Today I lead the imperial host in the open—I choose an honorable death over a shameful life.

sentences.zh: 但恨大將軍桓文之勳不遂，而兄一旦為逆節之臣，負先人平素之志，既沒之日，何顏見諸父于黃泉，謁先帝於地下邪？

translations.literal: Only I regret that the Grand General's merit like Huan and Wen will not be realized, while elder brother in one morning becomes a minister of rebellious principle, betraying the late elders' lifelong aim—when you go beneath, with what face will you see the fathers in the Yellow Springs or bow to the late Emperor underground?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun might have been another Duke Huan; you will enter history as traitors—how will you face our fathers in the grave?

sentences.zh: 執省來告，為兄羞之，且悲且慚。

translations.literal: Holding and reading your report shames me for you; I am both grieved and humiliated.
translations.idiomatic: Your letter leaves me ashamed for our name.

sentences.zh: 願速建大計，惟取錢鳳一人，使天下獲安，家國有福，故是竹素之事，非惟免禍而已。

translations.literal: I beg you swiftly to settle a great plan—only take Qian Feng one man—so that within the four seas there is peace, house and state have blessing; thus it will be a matter for bamboo and silk, not merely escaping disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Cut out Qian Feng alone, turn the army around, and you win peace and a place in the chronicles—not just survival.

sentences.zh: 夫福如反手，用之即是。

translations.literal: Fortune is like turning the hand—use it and it is there.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune is there for the taking if you seize it now.

sentences.zh: 導所統六軍，石頭萬五千人，宮內後苑二萬人，護軍屯金城六千人，劉遐已至，征北昨已濟江萬五千人。

translations.literal: The six armies Dao commands: fifteen thousand at Stone City, twenty thousand in the inner palace rear park, six thousand garrisoning Protector troops at Jincheng—Liu Xia has already arrived, and the army that conquered the north yesterday crossed the river, fifteen thousand.
translations.idiomatic: My tally: fifteen thousand at Stone Fortress, twenty thousand in the rear palaces, six thousand gold-wall guards, Liu Xia on the field, another fifteen thousand just crossed the river.

sentences.zh: 以天子之威，文武畢力，豈可當乎！

translations.literal: With the Son of Heaven's majesty and civil and military giving full strength—how could it be withstood!
translations.idiomatic: Against heaven's army at full strength you cannot stand!

sentences.zh: 事猶可追，兄早思之。

translations.literal: The affair may still be retrieved; elder brother, think early.
translations.idiomatic: You can still step back—decide now.

sentences.zh: 大兵一奪，導以為灼炟也。

translations.literal: Once great arms clash, Dao considers it blazing ruin.
translations.idiomatic: If steel meets steel, I tell you the realm burns.

sentences.zh: 含不答。

translations.literal: Han did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han did not answer.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中軍司馬曹渾等擊含於越城，含軍敗，敦聞，怒曰：「我兄老婢耳，門戶衰矣！

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Central Army Major Cao Hun and others to strike Han at Yuecheng; Han's army was defeated. When Dun heard it, he angrily said, "My elder brother is an old maidservant—our gate is ruined!
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi hit Wang Han at Yuecheng; Wang Dun raged, "My brother fights like a tired old woman—the clan is finished!

sentences.zh: 兄弟才兼文武者，世將、處季皆早死，今世事去矣。

translations.literal: Among brothers with talent spanning civil and military, Shijiang and Chuji both died early; now the age's affair is gone.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers who mattered—Shijiang, Chuji—are dead; the moment is lost.

sentences.zh: 」語參軍呂寶曰：「我當力行。

translations.literal: " He told his adjutant Lü Bao, "I ought to force myself to rise."
translations.idiomatic: He told his aide Lü Bao, "I must get up."

sentences.zh: 」因作勢而起，困乏復臥。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he made a motion to rise, but exhausted, lay down again.
translations.idiomatic: He tried to stand and collapsed back on the couch.

sentences.zh: 鳳等至京師，屯于水南。

translations.literal: Feng and the others reached the capital region and camped south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Feng's host camped south of the Qinhuai.

sentences.zh: 帝親率六軍以禦鳳，頻戰破之。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally led the six armies to oppose Feng and repeatedly fought and broke him.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi led the guards himself and broke Qian Feng again and again.

sentences.zh: 敦謂羊鑒及子應曰：「我亡後，應便即位，先立朝廷百官，然後乃營葬事。

translations.literal: Dun told Yang Jian and his son Ying, "After I die, Ying shall at once take the throne, first establish the court's hundred officials, and only then arrange burial."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun told Yang Jian and Wang Ying to enthrone the heir immediately, staff the bureaucracy, then bury him.

sentences.zh: 」初，敦始病，夢白犬自天而下齧之，又見刁協乘軺車導從，瞋目令左右執之。

translations.literal: At first, when Dun first fell ill, he dreamed a white dog descended from heaven and bit him; he also saw Diao Xie in a light cart with escort, glaring and ordering attendants to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: When illness began he dreamed a white dog fell from heaven to bite him; Diao Xie appeared in a carriage ordering his arrest.

sentences.zh: 俄而敦死，時年五十九。

translations.literal: Before long Dun died, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 應秘不發喪，裹屍以席，蠟塗其外，埋於廳事中，與諸葛瑤等恆縱酒淫樂。

translations.literal: Ying secretly did not announce the death; he wrapped the corpse in mats, coated the outside with wax, buried it in the main hall, and with Zhuge Yao and others constantly indulged in wine and debauchery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ying hid the corpse—mat-wrapped, wax-sealed, buried under the hall—while he and Zhuge Yao feasted and debauched.

sentences.zh: 沈充自吳率眾萬餘人至，與含等合。

translations.literal: Shen Chong came from Wu leading more than ten thousand men and joined Han and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chong marched from Wu with ten thousand and linked up with Wang Han.

sentences.zh: 充司馬顧揚說充曰：「今舉大事，而天子已扼其喉，情離眾沮，鋒摧勢挫，持疑猶豫，必致禍敗。

translations.literal: Chong's major Gu Yang advised Chong, saying, "Now we raise a great affair, yet the Son of Heaven already has us by the throat; feeling estranged, the host disheartened, edge broken and momentum checked—if we hesitate in doubt, we are sure to meet disaster and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: His officer Gu Yang warned, "The emperor has you by the throat; morale is gone—hesitate and you lose.

sentences.zh: 今若決破柵塘，因湖水灌京邑，肆舟檻之勢，極水軍之用，此所謂不戰而屈人之兵，上策也。

translations.literal: Now if we break the palisade and dikes and use lake water to flood the capital, exploit the advantage of hulls and oars and exhaust naval strength—this is what is called subduing another's soldiers without battle; it is the upper plan.
translations.idiomatic: Flood the capital by breaching the dikes—win without a pitched battle—that is best.

sentences.zh: 籍初至之銳，並東南眾軍之力，十道俱進，眾寡過倍，理必摧陷，中策也。

translations.literal: Relying on the keenness of first arrival together with the strength of the southeast hosts, ten routes advancing together, many times overmatching the few—by principle they are sure to be crushed; it is the middle plan.
translations.idiomatic: Strike on fresh valor with every southeastern column—the middle path.

sentences.zh: 轉禍為福，因敗為成，召錢鳳計事，因斬之以降，下策也。

translations.literal: To turn disaster into fortune and defeat into success, summon Qian Feng to consult on affairs and thereupon behead him to surrender—that is the lower plan.
translations.idiomatic: Murder Qian Feng and defect—that is the coward's gambit.

sentences.zh: 」充不能用，揚逃歸於吳。

translations.literal: " Chong could not use this; Yang fled back to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chong ignored him; Gu Yang ran home to Wu.

sentences.zh: 含復率眾渡淮，蘇峻等逆擊，大敗之，充亦燒營而退。

translations.literal: Han again led the host across the Huai; Su Jun and others met and struck them, greatly defeating them; Chong also burned camp and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han recrossed the Huai; Su Jun shattered him; Shen Chong torched his camp and fled.

sentences.zh: 既而周光斬錢鳳，吳儒斬沈充，並傳首京師。

translations.literal: Before long Zhou Guang beheaded Qian Feng, and Wu Ru beheaded Shen Chong; both sent heads to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Guang killed Qian Feng; Wu Ru killed Shen Chong—both heads went to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 有司議曰：「王敦滔天作逆，有無君之心，宜依崔杼、王浚故事，剖棺戮屍，以彰元惡。

translations.literal: The relevant officials deliberated, saying, "Wang Dun rebelled against heaven; he had a mind that did not acknowledge his lord—he should follow the precedents of Cui Zhu and Wang Jun, open the coffin and mutilate the corpse, to display the arch-evildoer.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry voted to drag Wang Dun from the grave like Cui Zhu's victim—open the coffin and hack the corpse.

sentences.zh: 」於是發瘞出屍，焚其衣冠，跽而刑之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they dug up the burial, brought out the corpse, burned his cap and gown, knelt him and punished him.
translations.idiomatic: They exhumed the body, burned his robes, and posthumously "executed" him.

sentences.zh: 敦、充首同日懸于南桁，觀者莫不稱慶。

translations.literal: Dun's and Chong's heads the same day were hung on the southern bridge; observers none failed to rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun's and Shen Chong's heads hung from the southern stockade while crowds cheered.

sentences.zh: 敦首既懸，莫敢收葬者。

translations.literal: Once Dun's head hung, none dared collect and bury it.
translations.idiomatic: No one dared claim Wang Dun's head for burial.

sentences.zh: 尚書令郗鑒言於帝曰：「昔王莽漆頭以輗車，董卓然腹以照市，王淩儭土，徐馥焚首。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Chi Jian spoke to the Emperor, saying, "Of old Wang Mang's head was lacquered for the prison cart, Dong Zhuo's belly was set alight to light the market, Wang Ling was exposed in earth, Xu Fu's head was burned.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Jian cited Wang Mang, Dong Zhuo, and others—state mutilation versus private burial.

sentences.zh: 前朝誅楊駿等，皆先極官刑，後聽私殯。

translations.literal: In the previous court Yang Jun and the rest were executed, all first given extreme official punishment, then private burial was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun's clique suffered public torture first, then kin could bury them.

sentences.zh: 然《春秋》許齊襄之葬紀侯，魏武義王修之哭袁譚。

translations.literal: Yet the 《Spring and Autumn》 permits Duke Xiang of Qi's burial of the Marquis of Ji, and Cao Cao honored Wang Xiu's weeping for Yuan Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the 《Spring and Autumn》 praises Qi for burying the lord of Ji; Cao Cao respected Wang Xiu mourning Yuan Tan.

sentences.zh: 由斯言之，王誅加於上，私義行於下。

translations.literal: From this speaking, royal punishment applies above, private duty may be practiced below.
translations.idiomatic: Public justice and private decency can coexist.

sentences.zh: 臣以為可聽私葬，於義為弘。

translations.literal: Your subject thinks private burial may be permitted; in right principle it is magnanimous.
translations.idiomatic: I say let the family bury him—magnanimous and right.

sentences.zh: 」昭許之，於是敦家收葬焉。

translations.literal: " The edict granted it; thereupon Dun's family collected and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed; the Wangs buried Wang Dun.

sentences.zh: 含父子乘單船奔荊州刺史王舒，舒使人沈之于江，餘黨悉平。

translations.literal: Han father and son took a single boat and fled to Governor of Jing Province Wang Shu; Shu had men sink them in the river; the remaining partisans were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han and his son fled to Wang Shu, who drowned them in the Yangzi; the rebellion ended.

sentences.zh: 敦眉目疏朗，性簡脫，有鑒裁，學通《左氏》，口不言財利，尤好清談，時人莫知，惟族兄戎異之。

translations.literal: Dun's brows and eyes were open and clear; his nature was simple and unbound; he had judgment and discernment; his learning penetrated the 《Zuo Tradition》; he spoke never of wealth or profit; he especially loved pure conversation—men of the time did not understand him; only his elder cousin on the clan Rong thought him extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun looked keen and open, mastered the 《Zuo Tradition》, feigned disdain for money, and shone at Pure Talk—only Wang Rong saw through him.

sentences.zh: 經略指麾，千里之外肅然，而麾下擾而不能整。

translations.literal: In strategy and command, beyond a thousand li all was orderly, yet under his command there was turmoil he could not set in order.
translations.idiomatic: He could move armies a thousand li away, yet could not discipline his own camp.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗召時賢共言伎藝之事，人人皆有所說，惟敦都無所關，意色殊惡。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once summoned the worthies of the time to speak together on skills and arts; every man had something to say; only Dun had no connection to any of it, his expression and color quite ugly.
translations.idiomatic: At a court talent show Wang Dun alone sneered and stayed silent—his face dark with contempt.

sentences.zh: 自言知擊鼓，因振袖揚枹，音節諧韻，神氣自得，傍若無人，舉坐歎其雄爽。

translations.literal: He said he knew how to beat drums; thereupon he shook his sleeves and raised the mallet; rhythm and tone were harmonious; spirit and bearing were self-satisfied, as if no one else were beside him—the whole company sighed at his heroic forthrightness.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed the war-drums instead, lifted the sticks, and brought down the house—guests called it bravado.

sentences.zh: 石崇以奢豪矜物，廁上常有十餘婢侍列，皆有容色，置甲煎粉、沈香汁，有如廁者，皆易新衣而出。

translations.literal: Shi Chong, arrogant in luxury, looked down on others; in his privy more than ten maidservants usually stood in attendance, all with pleasing looks; he set out nail paste and aloes wash; if someone used the privy, they all changed to new clothes before coming out.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chong lined his lavatory with ten perfumed maids and fresh robes for every visitor.

sentences.zh: 客多羞脫衣，而敦脫故著新，意色無怍。

translations.literal: Guests mostly were ashamed to strip clothes, yet Dun stripped his old ones and put on new ones, expression and color without shame.
translations.idiomatic: Guests blushed to undress; Wang Dun changed without a flicker of embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 群婢相謂曰：「此客必能作賊。

translations.literal: The maidservants said to one another, "This guest is sure to be able to become a bandit."
translations.idiomatic: The girls whispered, "That man could turn bandit."

sentences.zh: 」又嘗荒恣於色，體為之弊，左右諫之，敦曰：「此甚易耳。

translations.literal: " He also once wantonly indulged in sex until his body was harmed; attendants remonstrated; Dun said, "This is very easy."
translations.idiomatic: When excesses ruined his health and aides protested, he said, "Easy to fix."

sentences.zh: 」乃開後閣，驅諸婢妾數十人並放之，時人歎異焉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he opened the rear quarters, drove out several tens of concubines and slave girls together and released them; men of the time sighed in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: He emptied his harem onto the street—people marveled at the gesture.

translations.literal: The transmitted text carries a lone equals sign with no classical clause, likely a collation or import artifact.
translations.idiomatic: The received chapter here shows a stray equals sign—probably a formatting glitch, not words to translate.

sentences.zh: 沈充

translations.literal: Shen Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Biography: Shen Chong.

translations.literal: The transmitted line is a lone equals sign with no classical wording, likely an import artifact.
translations.idiomatic: Another stray equals sign appears in the edition—not readable text.

sentences.zh: 沈充，字士居。

translations.literal: Shen Chong, styled Shiju.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chong, courtesy name Shiju.

sentences.zh: 少好兵書，頗以雄豪聞於鄉里。

translations.literal: In youth he loved military texts and was somewhat renowned in his home district for heroic boldness.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he devoured military classics and locals already spoke of his swagger.

sentences.zh: 敦引為參軍，充因薦同郡錢鳳。

translations.literal: Dun appointed him clerk; Chong thereupon recommended Qian Feng of the same commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun made him an aide; Shen Chong pushed his countryman Qian Feng forward.

sentences.zh: 鳳字世儀，敦以為鎧曹參軍，數得進見。

translations.literal: Feng, styled Shiyi, Dun made Armor Bureau clerk; he repeatedly gained entry to audience.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Shiyi became Wang Dun's armory clerk and haunted the inner chambers.

sentences.zh: 知敦有不臣之心，因進邪說，遂相朋構，專弄威權，言成禍福。

translations.literal: Knowing Dun harbored a mind not of a subject, he advanced wicked talk; thereupon they formed a factional plot, monopolized awe-inspiring power, and his words decided blessing or disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Wang Dun's disloyalty, Qian Feng fed him poison counsel until they ran the court by whispers.

sentences.zh: 遭父喪，外托還葬，而密為敦使，與充交構。

translations.literal: When he met his father's mourning, outwardly he claimed to return for burial, but secretly he was Dun's envoy and wove intrigue with Chong.
translations.idiomatic: He used his father's funeral as cover while carrying secret orders between Wang Dun and Shen Chong.

sentences.zh: 初，敦參軍熊甫見敦委任鳳，將有異圖，因酒酣謂敦曰：「開國承家，小人勿用，佞幸在位，鮮不敗業。

translations.literal: At first Dun's clerk Xiong Fu, seeing Dun entrust Feng and about to harbor irregular designs, when the wine was deep said to Dun, "Founding state and inheriting house—do not employ petty men; when flatterers hold place, few do not ruin the enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Aide Xiong Fu, drunk, warned Wang Dun: "Petty men ruin houses—flatterers on the payroll mean collapse."

sentences.zh: 」敦作色曰：「小人阿誰？

translations.literal: " Dun changed color and said, "Which petty man?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun snarled, "Whom do you mean?"

sentences.zh: 」甫無懼容，因此告歸。

translations.literal: " Fu had no fearful look and on this account requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Fu stared him down and quit.

sentences.zh: 臨與敦別，因歌曰：「徂風飆起蓋山陵，氛霧蔽日玉石焚。

translations.literal: When parting from Dun he therefore sang, "Blast winds rise and mantle hill and mound; mist veils the sun, jade and stone burn.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving, he sang of storms burying hills—jade and stone consumed in flame.

sentences.zh: 往事既去可長歎，念別惆悵復會難。

translations.literal: The past gone, one may long sigh; thinking of parting, melancholy—meeting again is hard.
translations.idiomatic: The past is ash; parting aches because reunion is rare.

sentences.zh: 」敦知其諷己而不納。

translations.literal: " Dun knew he was satirizing himself but did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun knew the barb and ignored it.

sentences.zh: 明帝將伐敦，遣其鄉人沈禎諭充，許以為司空。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming was about to campaign against Dun, he sent Chong's fellow townsman Shen Zhen to instruct Chong, promising to make him Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming sent Shen Zhen, a townsman of Shen Chong, to offer him the ministry of works if he turned.

sentences.zh: 充謂禎曰：「三司具瞻之重，豈吾所任！

translations.literal: Chong said to Zhen, "The three excellencies' weight that all look up to—how could I bear such a post!"
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chong said, "A seat among the three councils is not for me."

sentences.zh: 幣厚言甘，古人所畏。

translations.literal: Thick gifts and sweet words are what the ancients feared.
translations.idiomatic: Sweet talk and fat bribes scared our forebears for good reason.

sentences.zh: 且丈夫共事，終始當同，寧可中道改易，人誰容我！

translations.literal: Moreover when men work together they should share beginning and end—how could I change course midway—who would forgive me!"
translations.idiomatic: We swore one path; break it and no one trusts me again."

sentences.zh: 」禎曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Zhen said, "It is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zhen said, "Wrong.

sentences.zh: 舍忠與順，未有不亡者也。

translations.literal: To abandon loyalty and compliance—none who do so fail to perish.
translations.idiomatic: Turn your back on loyalty and you perish.

sentences.zh: 大將軍阻兵不朝，爵賞自己，五尺之童知其異志。

translations.literal: The Grand General holds his troops and does not attend court; enfeoffments and rewards come from himself—even a child five feet tall knows his different intent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun shuns court and sells offices—even children see the coup coming.

sentences.zh: 今此之舉，將行篡弑耳，豈同於往年乎？

translations.literal: Now this movement will carry out usurpation and regicide—how can it match former years?
translations.idiomatic: This march aims at the throne, not another spat like before.

sentences.zh: 是以疆場諸將莫不歸赴本朝，內外之士咸願致死，正以移國易主，義不北面以事之也，奈何協同逆圖，當不義之責乎！

translations.literal: Therefore the generals on the borders none fail to hurry to the royal court; men within and without all wish to give their lives—precisely because the state would change masters and right principle forbids turning north to serve him—how can you join a treasonous plot and bear unrighteous blame!"
translations.idiomatic: Every garrison rallies to the emperor; no one will serve a usurper—why chain yourself to treason?"

sentences.zh: 朝廷坦誠，禎所知也。

translations.literal: The court's openness is what Zhen knows.
translations.idiomatic: I know the throne keeps its word.

sentences.zh: 賊之黨類，猶宥其罪，與之更始，況見機而作邪！

translations.literal: Even the villain's clique is still pardoned their crimes and given renewal—how much more one who sees the moment and acts!"
translations.idiomatic: Even Wang Dun's men get amnesty—why not you?"

sentences.zh: 」充不納。

translations.literal: " Chong did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chong refused.

sentences.zh: 率兵臨發，謂其妻子曰：「男兒不豎豹尾，終不還也。

translations.literal: Leading troops on the eve of departure, he told his wife and children, "A man who does not raise the leopard-tail banner will never return."
translations.idiomatic: He told his family he would not come home without a general's triumph.

sentences.zh: 」及敗歸吳興，亡失道，誤入其故將吳儒家。

translations.literal: " When defeated he returned toward Wuxing, lost the way, and mistakenly entered the house of his former officer Wu Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing defeat he lost his way and stumbled into Wu Ru's farm.

sentences.zh: 儒誘充內重壁中，因笑謂充曰：「三千戶侯也。

translations.literal: Ru lured Chong inside the layered wall and, laughing, said to Chong, "A marquis of three thousand households."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ru trapped him and grinned, "Here is my three-thousand-household prize."

sentences.zh: 」充曰：「封侯不足貪也。

translations.literal: " Chong said, "Marquis is not worth greed.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chong said, "I care nothing for a noble rank.

sentences.zh: 爾以大義存我，我宗族必厚報汝。

translations.literal: If you keep me alive for great right principle, my clan will surely repay you thickly.
translations.idiomatic: Spare me for honor's sake and my kin will reward you.

sentences.zh: 若必殺我，汝族滅矣。

translations.literal: If you must kill me, your clan will be exterminated."
translations.idiomatic: Kill me and your line dies."

sentences.zh: 」儒遂殺之。

translations.literal: " Ru thereupon killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ru cut his throat.

sentences.zh: 充子勁竟滅吳氏。

translations.literal: Chong's son Jin in the end extinguished the Wu clan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shen Jin later wiped out the Wu family.

sentences.zh: 勁見《忠義傳》。

translations.literal: Jin is seen in the "Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: Shen Jin appears in the biographies of the loyal and righteous.

sentences.zh: :史臣曰：琅邪之初鎮建鄴，龍德猶潛，雖當璧膺圖預定於冥兆，豐功厚利未被于黎氓。

translations.literal: The historiographers say: When Langya first garrisoned Jianye, dragon virtue was still hidden; though receiving the jade disk and bearing the chart had been fixed in dark portents, abundant merit and thick benefit had not yet reached the black-haired people.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: when the Jin court first settled Jiankang, the true Son of Heaven was still in shadow—omen spoke of the mandate, yet the people felt no blessing.

sentences.zh: 王敦曆官中朝，威名夙著，作牧淮海，望實逾隆，遂能托魚水之深期，定金蘭之密契，弼成王度，光佐中興，卜世延百二之期，論都創三分之業，此功固不細也。

translations.literal: Wang Dun had long served the central court, his awe-inspiring name noted from of old; as shepherd of Huai and Hai his repute and substance grew higher; thus he could rely on a deep expectation like fish and water, fix a secret pact like metal and orchid, assist in completing royal measure, and brilliantly aid the restoration—divining the age to extend the "hundred and two" span, debating the capital to found enterprise in three parts—this achievement was indeed not slight.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun came south with a statesman's résumé, won Sima Rui's trust, and built the Eastern Jin—no small feat.

sentences.zh: 既而負勳高而圖非望，恃勢逼而肆驕陵。

translations.literal: Then he bore high merit and plotted illegitimate hope; relying on coercive power he indulged arrogant bullying.
translations.idiomatic: Then pride drove him to reach past the throne; force made him cruel.

sentences.zh: 釁隙起自刁劉，禍難成于錢沈。

translations.literal: The rift rose from Diao and Liu; disaster matured with Qian and Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Xie and Liu Kui sparked the split; Qian Feng and Shen Chong finished it.

sentences.zh: 興晉陽之甲，纏象魏之兵。

translations.literal: He raised the hosts of Jinyang and wrapped the capital in war.
translations.idiomatic: He marched like the lords who "arm Jinyang" and besieged the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 蜂目既露，豺聲又發，擅竊國命，殺害忠良，遂欲篡盜乘輿，逼遷龜鼎。

translations.literal: The wasp eyes already showed, the jackal voice sounded again; he stole the state mandate without right, killed the loyal and good; then he wished to usurp the imperial carriage and force the sacred tripods to move.
translations.idiomatic: The wasp eyes and jackal voice Pan Tao foretold came true—he seized power, slaughtered ministers, and aimed at the throne.

sentences.zh: 賴嗣君英略，晉祚靈長，諸侯釋位，股肱戮力，用能運茲廟算，殄彼凶徒，克固鴻圖，載清天步者矣。

translations.literal: Thanks to the heir's heroic strategy, Jin's fortune was numinously long; the feudal lords released their stations and the thigh-and-arm ministers exerted strength—thereby they could wield such temple calculations, exterminate those vicious followers, secure the great plan, and clear the heavenly step.
translations.idiomatic: The young emperor rallied the realm; lords and generals struck back—thus the traitors fell and the dynasty stood.

sentences.zh: 桓溫

translations.literal: Huan Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Biography: Huan Wen.

sentences.zh: 桓溫，字元子，宣城太守彝之子也。

translations.literal: Huan Wen, styled Yuanzi, was the son of Administrator of Xuancheng Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen, courtesy name Yuanzi, was Huan Yi's son.

sentences.zh: 生未期而太原溫嶠見之，曰：「此兒有奇骨，可試使啼。

translations.literal: Before he was one year old, Wen Jiao of Taiyuan saw him and said, "This child has extraordinary bones; try to make him cry."
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan's Wen Jiao saw the infant and said, "Fine bones—make him cry."

sentences.zh: 」及聞其聲，曰：「真英物也！

translations.literal: " When he heard the sound, he said, "Truly a heroic creature!"
translations.idiomatic: When the baby wailed, Wen Jiao cried, "A born champion!"

sentences.zh: 」以嶠所賞，故遂名之曰溫。

translations.literal: " Because Jiao admired him, he therefore named him Wen.
translations.idiomatic: So the boy took Wen from Wen Jiao's name.

sentences.zh: 嶠笑曰：「果爾，後將易吾姓也。

translations.literal: " Jiao laughed and said, "If it is so, later he will change my surname."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Jiao joked, "Then one day he will steal my surname too."

sentences.zh: 」彝為韓晃所害，涇令江播豫焉。

translations.literal: " Yi was killed by Han Huang; Magistrate of Jing Jiang Bo was complicit.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yi died to Han Huang; Magistrate Jiang Bo of Jing helped plot it.

sentences.zh: 溫時年十五，枕戈泣血，志在復仇。

translations.literal: Wen was then fifteen; he pillow-speared and wept blood, his aim set on revenge.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen Huan Wen slept on a spear and swore blood vengeance.

sentences.zh: 至年十八，會播已終，子彪兄弟三人居喪，置刃杖中，以為溫備。

translations.literal: When he reached eighteen, it happened that Bo had already died; Biao and his two younger brothers were in mourning, placed blades in the staff, preparing for Wen.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen Jiang Bo was dead; his three sons mourned with daggers hidden in their mourning staffs.

sentences.zh: 溫詭稱吊賓，得進，刃彪於廬中，並追二弟殺之，時人稱焉。

translations.literal: Wen falsely claimed to be a condolence guest, gained entry, stabbed Biao in the hut, and pursued and killed the two younger brothers—men of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen posed as a mourner, knifed the eldest in the shed, ran down the brothers—people admired the vendetta.

sentences.zh: 溫豪爽有風概，姿貌甚偉，面有七星。

translations.literal: Wen was bold and forthright in manner, with striking bearing; his face had seven star marks.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen was tall, striking, with seven moles like a constellation on his cheek.

sentences.zh: 少與沛國劉惔善，惔嘗稱之曰：「溫眼如紫石棱，須作猥毛磔，孫仲謀、晉宣王之流亞也。

translations.literal: In youth he was friendly with Liu Tan of Pei; Tan once praised him, saying, "Wen's eyes are like purple-quartz facets, his beard bristles like boar bristle—he is in the class of Sun Quan and Sima Yi."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tan said his eyes flashed like amethyst, his beard like Sun Quan's or Sima Yi's.

sentences.zh: 」選尚南康長公主，拜駙馬都尉，襲爵萬寧男，除琅邪太守，累遷徐州刺史。

translations.literal: " He was selected to marry Princess of Nankang, the elder princess, was appointed Commandant of the Household for the Imperial Son-in-Law, inherited the noble rank of Baron of Wanning, was given Langya Administrator, and was promoted in stages to Governor of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He married the princess, became son-in-law commandant, baron of Wanning, then governor of Xu.

sentences.zh: 溫與庾翼友善，恆相期以寧濟之事。

translations.literal: Wen was friendly with Yu Yi and constantly looked to each other for the task of pacifying and aiding the age.
translations.idiomatic: He and Yu Yi dreamed together of saving the realm.

sentences.zh: 翼嘗薦溫於明帝曰；

translations.literal: Yi once recommended Wen to Emperor Ming, saying;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi once told Emperor Ming:

sentences.zh: 「桓溫少有雄略，願陛下勿以常人遇之，常婿畜之，宜委以方召之任，托其弘濟艱難之勳。

translations.literal: "Huan Wen in youth has heroic strategy; I beg Your Majesty not to treat him as an ordinary man or rear him as an ordinary son-in-law—you should entrust him with the duty of a regional commander and rely on him for the merit of broadly aiding this hardship."
translations.idiomatic: Do not treat Huan Wen as a decorative son-in-law—give him a frontier command and hard work."

sentences.zh: 」翼卒，以溫為都督荊梁四州諸軍事、安西將軍、荊州刺史、領護南蠻校尉、假節。

translations.literal: " When Yi died, Wen was made area commander for Jing, Liang, and four other provinces' military affairs, General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Jing Province, concurrent chief of the southern Man, and invested with the staff of authority.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Yi died, Huan Wen took Jing and four provinces, with the western command and credential staff.

sentences.zh: 時李勢微弱，溫志在立勳於蜀，，率眾西伐。

translations.literal: At the time Li Shi was weak; Wen's aim was to establish merit in Shu; he led the host west to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi's Shu was feeble; Huan Wen marched west for glory.

sentences.zh: 時康獻太后臨朝，溫將發，上疏而行。

translations.literal: At the time Empress Dowager Kang-Xian held court; when Wen was about to set out, he submitted a memorial and then marched.
translations.idiomatic: Under the regent empress he filed a memorial and left.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以蜀險遠，而溫兵寡少，深入敵場，甚以為憂。

translations.literal: The court thought Shu perilous and distant, while Wen's troops were few and thin; to penetrate deep into enemy ground was greatly worrisome.
translations.idiomatic: Jiankang feared the depth of Shu and the thinness of his column.

sentences.zh: 初，諸葛亮造八陣圖于魚復平沙之上，壘石為八行，行相去二丈。

translations.literal: At first Zhuge Liang had built the Eight Formations Diagram on the sand flats at Yufu, piling stones in eight rows, two zhang apart between rows.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang's stone maze still lay on the Yufu sands—eight rows two yards apart.

sentences.zh: 溫見之，謂「此常山蛇勢也。

translations.literal: When Wen saw it, he said, "This is the 'Mount Chang serpent' formation."
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen recognized the "Mount Chang snake" deployment.

sentences.zh: 」文武皆莫能識之。

translations.literal: " Civil and military none could understand it.
translations.idiomatic: His staff could not read the pattern.

sentences.zh: 及軍次彭模，乃命參軍周楚、孫盛守輜重，自將步卒直指成都。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Pengmo, he ordered clerks Zhou Chu and Sun Sheng to guard baggage; he personally led foot soldiers straight toward Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: At Pengmo he left Zhou Chu and Sun Sheng with the train and drove on foot for Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 勢使其叔父福及從兄權等攻彭模，楚等禦之，福退走。

translations.literal: Shi had his uncle Fu and cousin Quan and others attack Pengmo; Chu and the others resisted; Fu retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi's uncle Li Fu attacked; Zhou Chu held; Li Fu fled.

sentences.zh: 溫又擊權等，三戰三捷，賊眾散，自間道歸成都。

translations.literal: Wen again struck Quan and the others, three battles three victories; the bandit host scattered and returned to Chengdu by hidden paths.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen routed Li Quan three times; the Shu army melted toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 勢於是悉眾與溫戰於笮橋，參軍龔護戰沒，眾懼欲退，而鼓吏誤鳴進鼓，於是攻之，勢眾大潰。

translations.literal: Shi thereupon led the full host and fought Wen at Zhu Bridge; clerk Gong Hu died in battle; the host feared and wished to withdraw, but the drum officer mistakenly sounded the advance drum; thereupon they attacked; Shi's host was greatly routed.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhu Bridge Gong Hu fell; the Jin line faltered until a drummer hit the wrong beat and sent them forward—Shu collapsed.

sentences.zh: 溫乘勝直進，焚其小城，勢遂夜遁九十里，至晉壽葭萌城，其將鄧嵩、昝堅勸勢降，乃面縛輿櫬請命。

translations.literal: Wen pressed the victory straight in, burned the small city; Shi then fled by night ninety li to Jinshou at the Jiameng citadel; his generals Deng Song and Zan Jian urged Shi to surrender; thereupon with face bound and coffin on cart he begged for his life.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen burned the outworks; Li Shi ran to Jiameng, then surrendered in ropes beside a bier.

sentences.zh: 溫解縛焚櫬，送于京師。

translations.literal: Wen loosed the bonds and burned the coffin and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen freed him, burned the death-bier, and sent him east.

sentences.zh: 溫停蜀三旬，舉賢旌善，偽尚書僕射王誓、中書監王瑜、鎮東將軍鄧定、散騎常侍常璩等，皆蜀之良也，並以為參軍，百姓咸悅。

translations.literal: Wen stayed in Shu thirty days, raised the worthy and displayed the good; false Masters of Writing Wang Shi, Palace Secretariat Director Wang Yu, General Who Guards the East Deng Ding, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Chang Qu and others were all good men of Shu; he appointed them all clerks; the hundred surnames were all pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He spent a month in Shu enlisting talent—Wang Shi, Chang Qu, and others joined his staff; the people cheered.

sentences.zh: 軍未旋而王誓、鄧定、隗文等反，溫復討平之。

translations.literal: Before the army had rotated back Wang Shi, Deng Ding, Wei Wen, and others rebelled; Wen again campaigned and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh mutinies rose before he left; he crushed them.

sentences.zh: 振旅還江陵，進位征西大將軍、開府，封臨賀郡公。

translations.literal: He shook the host and returned to Jiangling, was advanced to Grand General Who Conquers the West, with opening of a separate office, and enfeoffed Duke of Linhe commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He marched back to Jiangling as grand general who conquers the west, duke of Linhe.

sentences.zh: 及石季龍死，溫欲率眾北征，先上疏求朝廷議水陸之宜，久不報。

translations.literal: When Shi Jilong died, Wen wished to lead the host north to campaign; first he submitted a memorial asking the court to deliberate suitability of water and land routes; long there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Hu's death Huan Wen demanded a northern campaign and a strategy session; the court stayed silent.

sentences.zh: 時知朝廷杖殷浩等以抗己，溫甚忿之，然素知浩，弗之憚也。

translations.literal: At the time it was known the court relied on Yin Hao and others to resist him; Wen was very resentful, yet he had long known Hao and did not fear him.
translations.idiomatic: The court propped up Yin Hao against him; Huan Wen fumed but did not fear the man.

sentences.zh: 以國無他釁，遂得相持彌年，雖有君臣之跡，亦相羈縻而已，八州士眾資調，殆不為國家用。

translations.literal: Because the state had no other quarrel, they were able to stand off for years; though traces of lord and minister remained, they were only mutually tethered—the levies and supplies of eight provinces' officers and people were almost not used for the state's purposes.
translations.idiomatic: Years of cold war followed while eight provinces' taxes fed Huan Wen, not the throne.

sentences.zh: 聲言北伐，拜表便行，順流而下，行達武昌，眾四五萬。

translations.literal: He declared a northern expedition, submitted his memorial and set out, went downstream, reached Wuchang with forty or fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He announced a northern drive, sailed to Wuchang with fifty thousand.

sentences.zh: 殷浩慮為溫所廢，將謀避之，又欲以騶虞幡住溫軍，內外噂，人情震駭。

translations.literal: Yin Hao feared Wen would depose him, planned to avoid it, and also wished to use the zouyu banner to halt Wen's army—inside and outside there was hubbub; human hearts were shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao plotted to stop him with a peace banner; the capital panicked.

sentences.zh: 簡文帝時為撫軍，與溫書明社稷大計，疑惑所由。

translations.literal: Prince Jianwen at the time was General Who Pacifies the Army; he wrote Wen clarifying the great plan of the altars and the source of suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yu, as general who pacifies the army, wrote urging clarity on state policy.

sentences.zh: 溫即回軍還鎮，上疏曰：

translations.literal: Wen immediately turned the army back to garrison and submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen about-faced and filed a memorial:

sentences.zh: :臣近親率所統，欲北掃趙魏，軍次武昌，獲撫軍大將軍、會稽王昱書，說風塵紛紜，妄生疑惑，辭旨危急，憂及社稷。

translations.literal: "Your subject lately led what he commands in person, intending to sweep north through Zhao and Wei; the army halted at Wuchang and received a letter from the General Who Pacifies the Army, Grand General, Prince of Kuaiji, Yu—speaking of wind and dust in confusion, groundless suspicion born, the tone urgent, worry reaching the altars.
translations.idiomatic: I marched for the north, stopped at Wuchang, and read Prince Yu's frantic letter about "dust in the capital" and danger to the state.

sentences.zh: 省之惋愕，不解所由，形影相顧，隕越無地。

translations.literal: Reading it I was startled and grieved, not understanding the reason; body and shadow looked at each other; I had no ground to stand on.
translations.idiomatic: I was stunned—what had I done to deserve this terror?"

sentences.zh: 臣以暗蔽，忝荷重任，雖才非其人，職在靜亂。

translations.literal: Your subject, in darkness and obscurity, disgracefully bears a heavy charge; though talent does not match the man, the office lies in quieting chaos.
translations.idiomatic: I am no genius, but my duty is to end turmoil.

sentences.zh: 寇仇不滅，國恥未雪，幸因開泰之期，遇可乘之會，匹夫有志，猶懷憤慨，臣亦何心，坐觀其弊！

translations.literal: The foe is not destroyed, national shame not washed away; fortunately in this open-great time we meet an opportunity that may be seized—even a common man cherishes indignation; how could your subject sit watching its harm!
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians still mock us—how can I sit idle?"

sentences.zh: 故荷戈驅馳，不遑寧處，前後表陳，於今歷年矣。

translations.literal: Therefore bearing spear and galloping, I have no leisure to rest; before and after I have memorialized—now it has been years.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year I have begged leave to march."

sentences.zh: 丹誠坦然，公私所察，有何纖介，容此嫌忌？

translations.literal: Crimson sincerity is open; public and private may inspect it—what hair's breadth could hold this suspicion and jealousy?
translations.idiomatic: My heart is bare—why invent plots?"

sentences.zh: 豈醜正之徒心懷怵惕，操弄虛說，以惑朝聽？

translations.literal: Could it be that crooked men who hate the upright harbor fear in their hearts, wielding empty talk to confuse the court's hearing?
translations.idiomatic: Petty men poison the ear of the throne."

sentences.zh: :昔樂毅謁誠，垂涕流奔，霍光盡忠，上官告變。

translations.literal: "Of old Yue Yi was utterly sincere, weeping as he fled; Huo Guang was utterly loyal; Shangguan raised a coup.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yi fled in tears; Huo Guang stayed loyal while Shangguan plotted."

sentences.zh: 讒說殄行，奸邪亂德，及歷代之常患，存亡之所由也。

translations.literal: Slanderous talk destroys conduct; wickedness and flattery disorder virtue—these are the constant ills of successive ages and the reason for survival or perishment.
translations.idiomatic: Slander kills—that is how dynasties fall."

sentences.zh: 今主上富於陽秋，陛下以聖淑臨朝，恭己委任，責成群下，方寄會通於群才，布德信於遐荒。

translations.literal: Now the lord above is rich in spring and autumn years; Your Majesty, with sagely virtue, faces the court, respectful and self-effacing in entrustment, laying blame on subordinates—you are just about to consign comprehensive governance to gathered talent and spread virtue and trust to distant wastes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is young; you govern with grace and delegate—yet rumor splits us."

sentences.zh: 況臣世蒙殊恩，服事三朝，身非羈旅之賓，跡無韓彭之釁，而反間起於胸心，交亂過於四國，此古賢所以歎息於既往，而臣亦大懼于當年也。

translations.literal: Moreover your subject's house has received extraordinary grace for generations, serving three courts; I am no guest in bonds, my tracks hold no Han-Xin or Peng Yue quarrel—yet estrangement rises in breasts and hearts, intrigue crosses worse than the four states—this is why the worthies of old sighed at what had passed, and your subject too greatly fears for the present year.
translations.idiomatic: My clan served three emperors loyally—no Han Xin guilt—still you suspect me worse than ancient cabals.

sentences.zh: 今橫議妄生，成此貝錦，使垂滅之賊復獲蘇息，所以痛心絕氣，悲慨彌深。

translations.literal: Now reckless talk arises at random, weaves this shell-pattern slander, letting the nearly extinguished foe revive and breathe—therefore I am heartsick and breath-cut, grief and indignation run deep.
translations.idiomatic: Lies revive our enemies—I choke on rage.

sentences.zh: 臣雖所存者公，所務者國；

translations.literal: Though what your subject harbors is public and what he pursues is the state,
translations.idiomatic: I serve the realm, not myself,

sentences.zh: 然外難未弭，而內弊交興，則臣本心陳力之志也。

translations.literal: yet outer peril is not removed while inner ills arise together—then it is your subject's original mind to offer his strength.
translations.idiomatic: yet infighting blocks the border—that is what I meant to cure.

sentences.zh: 進位太尉，固讓不拜。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Commandant but firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: They made him grand commandant; he refused.

sentences.zh: 時殷浩至洛陽修復園陵，經涉數年，屢戰屢敗，器械都盡。

translations.literal: At the time Yin Hao had reached Luoyang to repair the imperial tombs; he passed through several years, repeatedly fought and repeatedly failed, weapons exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao wasted years fixing Luoyang tombs and lost every battle.

sentences.zh: 溫復進督司州，因朝野之怨，乃奏廢浩，自此內外大權一歸溫矣。

translations.literal: Wen was further advanced to supervise Si Province; riding the court and countryside's resentment, he then memorialized to depose Hao—thereafter inner and outer great power all returned to Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen added Si Province, impeached Yin Hao on public fury, and swallowed the court.

sentences.zh: 溫遂統步騎四萬發江陵，水軍自襄陽入均口。

translations.literal: Wen thereupon commanded forty thousand foot and horse, setting out from Jiangling; the naval force entered Jun Ford from Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He led forty thousand from Jiangling; the fleet entered the Han from Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 至南鄉，步自淅川以征關中，命梁州刺史司馬勳出子午道。

translations.literal: Reaching Nanxiang, he went on foot from Xi River to campaign in Guanzhong; he ordered Governor of Liang Province Sima Xun out by the Ziwu road.
translations.idiomatic: At Nanxiang he struck overland into Guanzhong while Sima Xun took the Ziwu pass.

sentences.zh: 別軍攻上洛，獲苻健荊州刺史郭敬，進擊青泥，破之。

translations.literal: A separate column attacked Shangluo, captured Guo Jing, Jing Province governor under Fu Jian of Former Qin, advanced and struck Qingni, and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Another wing took Shangluo, seized Fu Jian's governor Guo Jing, and smashed the force at Qingni.

sentences.zh: 健又遣子生、弟雄眾數萬屯嶢柳、愁思塠以距溫，遂大戰，生親自陷陣，殺溫將應庭、劉泓，死傷千數。

translations.literal: Jian again sent his son Sheng and younger brother Xiong with a host of several tens of thousands to camp at Yaoliu and Chousidui to oppose Wen; there was a great battle; Sheng personally charged the line, killed Wen's generals Ying Ting and Liu Hong, and dead and wounded numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian sent Fu Sheng and Fu Xiong to block Huan Wen; Fu Sheng killed Jin generals Ying Ting and Liu Hong in a bloodbath.

sentences.zh: 溫軍力戰，生眾乃散。

translations.literal: Wen's army fought hard; Sheng's host then scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen's men broke Fu Sheng's line.

sentences.zh: 雄又與將軍桓沖戰白鹿原，又為沖所破。

translations.literal: Xiong again fought General Huan Chong at Bailuyuan and was again broken by Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xiong met Huan Chong on Bailuyuan and lost again.

sentences.zh: 雄遂馳襲司馬勳，勳退次女媧堡。

translations.literal: Xiong then galloped to strike Sima Xun; Xun retreated to station at Nüwabao.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xiong chased Sima Xun back to Nüwa redoubt.

sentences.zh: 溫進至霸上，健以五千人深溝自固，居人皆安堵復業，持牛酒迎溫于路者十八九，耆老感泣曰：「不圖今日復見官軍！

translations.literal: Wen advanced to Bashang; Jian with five thousand men dug deep moats and held fast; residents were all secure and resumed work; eight or nine of those who brought cattle and wine to welcome Wen on the road were elders who wept in gratitude, saying, "We did not expect today again to see government troops!"
translations.idiomatic: At Bashang the locals cheered Huan Wen—old men wept that imperial soldiers had returned.

sentences.zh: 」初，溫恃麥熟，取以為軍資。

translations.literal: " At first Wen had relied on the wheat ripening and took it for army supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen had counted on the wheat crop for supplies.

sentences.zh: 而健芟苗清野，軍糧不屬，收三千餘口而還。

translations.literal: But Jian cut the seedlings and cleared the fields; army grain did not connect; he gathered more than three thousand captives and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian scorched the earth; Huan Wen ran out of food and retreated with prisoners.

sentences.zh: 帝使侍中黃門勞溫於襄陽。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Palace Attendants and Gentlemen of the Yellow Gates to console Wen at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent envoys to comfort him at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 初，溫自以雄姿風氣是宣帝、劉琨之儔，有以其比王敦者，意甚不平。

translations.literal: At first Wen himself thought his heroic bearing was of the class of Emperor Xuan and Liu Kun; when someone compared him to Wang Dun, his mind was very unbalanced.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen fancied himself another Sima Yi or Liu Kun; any comparison to Wang Dun infuriated him.

sentences.zh: 及是征還，於北方得一巧作老婢，訪之，乃琨伎女也，一見溫，便潸然而泣。

translations.literal: When on this campaign he returned north, he obtained from the north a clever old bondmaid; questioning her, she turned out to be a musician of Kun's; at one sight of Wen she wept streaming tears.
translations.idiomatic: On the way back he bought an old slave woman who had served Liu Kun—she burst into tears at his face.

sentences.zh: 溫問其故，答曰：「公甚似劉司空。

translations.literal: Wen asked the reason; she answered, "My lord greatly resembles Minister Liu."
translations.idiomatic: She said he looked like Liu Kun.

sentences.zh: 」溫大悅，出外整理衣冠，又呼婢問。

translations.literal: " Wen was greatly pleased, went out to arrange cap and gown, and called the maid again to ask.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, he dressed up and made her look again.

sentences.zh: 婢云：「面甚似，恨薄；

translations.literal: The maid said, "The face greatly resembles—only it is too thin;
translations.idiomatic: She said his face matched—but too thin;

sentences.zh: 眼甚似，恨小；

translations.literal: the eyes greatly resemble—only they are too small;
translations.idiomatic: eyes matched—too small;

sentences.zh: 須甚似，恨赤；

translations.literal: the beard greatly resembles—only it is too ruddy;
translations.idiomatic: beard matched—too red;

sentences.zh: 形甚似，恨短；

translations.literal: the form greatly resembles—only it is too short;
translations.idiomatic: stature matched—too short;

sentences.zh: 聲甚似，恨雌。

translations.literal: the voice greatly resembles—only it is too soft."
translations.idiomatic: voice matched—too effeminate."

sentences.zh: 」溫於是褫冠解帶，昏然而睡，不怡者數日。

translations.literal: " Wen thereupon tore off cap and loosened belt, slept in a daze, and was displeased for several days.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen sulked for days.

sentences.zh: 母孔氏卒，上疏解職，欲送葬宛陵，詔不許。

translations.literal: When his mother Lady Kong died, he submitted a memorial asking to resign his post, wishing to escort burial to Wanling; an edict did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died; he begged to bury her at Wanling; the throne refused leave.

sentences.zh: 贈臨賀太夫人印綬，諡曰敬，遣侍中弔祭，謁者監護喪事，旬月之中，使者八至，軺軒相望於道。

translations.literal: She was posthumously given the Lady of Linhe's seal-cord, canonized Reverent; a palace attendant was sent to condole and sacrifice, a herald supervised the funeral—in the space of a month envoys arrived eight times; light carts lined the road.
translations.idiomatic: The court piled honors on Lady Kong—eight embassies in a month.

sentences.zh: 溫葬畢視事，欲修復園陵，移都洛陽，表疏十餘上，不許。

translations.literal: When Wen finished burial and took up affairs, he wished to repair the imperial tombs and move the capital to Luoyang; he submitted more than ten memorials; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to duty demanding Luoyang as capital and tomb repairs—ten memorials, ten refusals.

sentences.zh: 進溫征討大都督、督司冀二州諸軍事，委以專征之任。

translations.literal: Wen was advanced to Grand Area Commander for Conquest, area commander for Si and Ji provinces' military affairs, entrusted with sole campaigning authority.
translations.idiomatic: They named him supreme commander over Si and Ji with full war powers.

sentences.zh: 溫遣督護高武據魯陽，輔國將軍戴施屯河上，勒舟師以逼許洛，以譙梁水道既通，請徐豫兵乘淮泗入河。

translations.literal: Wen sent Protector Gao Wu to hold Luyang, General Who Supports the State Dai Shi to camp on the river, pressed a fleet to threaten Xu and Luoyang; because the Qiao-Liang waterway was already open, he asked for Xu and Yu troops to ride Huai and Si into the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: He strung out garrisons from Luyang to the Yellow River and asked for eastern reinforcements by water.

sentences.zh: 溫自江陵北伐，行經金城，見少為琅邪時所種柳皆已十圍，慨然曰：「木猶如此，人何以堪！

translations.literal: Wen campaigned north from Jiangling; passing Jincheng he saw willows he had planted in youth as Prince of Langya, now ten arm-spans round; he sighed, "Trees are thus—how can men bear it!"
translations.idiomatic: Passing Jincheng he saw his old willows grown huge and sighed, "Even trees age—what of men?"

sentences.zh: 」攀枝執條，泫然流涕。

translations.literal: " He grasped branches and held twigs, tears flowing.
translations.idiomatic: He wept on the branches.

sentences.zh: 於是過淮泗，踐北境，與諸僚屬登平乘樓，眺矚中原，慨然曰：「遂使神州陸沈，百年丘墟，王夷甫諸人不得不任其責！

translations.literal: Thereupon crossing Huai and Si, treading the northern frontier, he ascended the flat-ship tower with his staff, gazing out over the central plain; he sighed, "This has let the divine land sink, a hundred years of ruin—men like Wang Yanfu cannot escape their blame!"
translations.idiomatic: From the tower he cursed Wang Yan and the western Jin elite for losing the north.

sentences.zh: 」袁宏曰：「運有興廢，豈必諸人之過！

translations.literal: " Yuan Hong said, "Fortune has rise and fall—must it be those men's fault!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong said fate, not only men, shaped the fall.

sentences.zh: 」溫作色謂四座曰：「頗聞劉景升有千斤大牛，啖芻豆十倍于常牛，負重致遠，曾不若一羸牸，魏武入荊州，以享軍士。

translations.literal: " Wen changed color and told the company, "I have heard Liu Jingsheng had a thousand-jin ox that ate ten times ordinary cattle's fodder, yet bearing weight and going far it was not a match for one lean cow—when Wei Wu entered Jing Province he fed it to the army."
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen darkly compared Yuan Hong to Liu Biao's useless ox—Cao Cao had slaughtered for meat.

sentences.zh: 」意以況宏，坐中皆失色。

translations.literal: " His meaning likened Hong to it; all in the seat lost color.
translations.idiomatic: The bench went white.

sentences.zh: 師次伊水，姚襄屯水北，距水而戰。

translations.literal: The army halted on the Yi River; Yao Xiang camped north of the river and fought across the water.
translations.idiomatic: He met Yao Xiang at the Yi.

sentences.zh: 溫結陣而前，親被甲督弟沖及諸將奮擊，襄大敗，自相殺死者數千人，越北芒而西走，追之不及，遂奔平陽。

translations.literal: Wen formed battle lines and advanced, personally donning armor to supervise his younger brother Chong and the various generals in fierce attack; Xiang was greatly defeated, those who killed each other in the rout numbered several thousand; he fled west past Beimang; pursuit did not catch him, and he ran to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen shattered Yao Xiang; the rebel fled toward Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 溫屯故太極殿前，徙入金墉城，謁先帝諸陵，陵被侵毀者皆繕復之，兼置陵令。

translations.literal: Wen camped before the old Great Ultimate Hall, moved into the Jinyong citadel, visited the late emperors' tombs—those violated or ruined he all repaired—and concurrently set tomb wardens.
translations.idiomatic: He occupied Luoyang, patched the desecrated tombs, and posted wardens.

sentences.zh: 遂旋軍，執降賊周成以歸，遷降人三千餘家于江漢之間。

translations.literal: Thereupon he rotated the army, seized the surrendered bandit Zhou Cheng to return, and relocated more than three thousand surrendered households between the Yang and Han.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew with captive Zhou Cheng and resettled thousands south of the Han.

sentences.zh: 遣西陽太守滕畯出黃城，討蠻賊文盧等，又遣江夏相劉岵、義陽太守胡驥討妖賊李弘，皆破之，傳首京都。

translations.literal: He sent Xiyang Administrator Teng Jun out of Huangcheng to campaign against Man bandits Wen Lu and others, and also sent Jiangxia Chancellor Liu Hu and Yiyang Administrator Hu Ji to campaign against sorcerer-rebel Li Hong—all were broken and heads sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He mopped up bandits on the middle Yangzi and sent heads east.

sentences.zh: 溫還軍之後，司、豫、青、兗復陷於賊。

translations.literal: After Wen rotated the army, Si, Yu, Qing, and Yan again fell to bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Once he left, the north collapsed again.

sentences.zh: 升平中，改封南郡公，降臨賀為縣公，以封其次子濟。

translations.literal: In the Shengping era his fief was changed to Duke of Nan commandery; Linhe was demoted to county duke and given to enfeoff his second son Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He became duke of Nanjun; Linhe went to his son Huan Ji.

sentences.zh: 隆和初，寇逼河南，太守戴施出奔，冠軍將軍陳祐告急，溫使竟陵太守鄧遐率三千人助祐，並欲還都洛陽，上疏曰：

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longhe, invaders pressed Henan; Administrator Dai Shi fled; General Who Takes the Crown Chen You called for help; Wen sent Jingling Administrator Xia with three thousand men to aid You, and also wished to return the capital to Luoyang; he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Henan buckled, Huan Wen sent Deng Xia to Chen You and again demanded moving the court to Luoyang:

sentences.zh: :巴蜀既平，逆胡消滅，時來之會既至，休泰之慶顯著。

translations.literal: "Shu and Ba already pacified, the rebellious Hu extinguished—the moment has arrived and the blessing of peace is plain.
translations.idiomatic: Shu is quiet and the barbarians beaten—the time favors recovery.

sentences.zh: 而人事乖違，屢喪王略，復使二賊雙起，海內崩裂，河洛蕭條，山陵危逼，所以遐邇悲惶，痛心於既往者也。

translations.literal: Yet human affairs have gone awry and the kingly plan has repeatedly been lost, letting two foes rise together; within the seas it has split apart; He and Luo are desolate; the hills tombs are pressed in peril—therefore near and far mourn in panic, heartsore for what is past.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jin fumbled and the frontier split; the old capitals lie in ruins.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下稟乾坤自然之姿，挺羲皇玄朗之德，鳳棲外籓，龍飛皇極，時務陵替，備徹天聽，人之情偽，盡知之矣。

translations.literal: I prostrate myself in thought: Your Majesty bears the natural posture of Qian and Kun, stands forth with the bright virtue of Fuxi; the phoenix rested in an outer screen, the dragon flew to the supreme pivot; the age's tasks decline and all reaches heaven's hearing; the people's truth and falsehood you fully know.
translations.idiomatic: You carry heaven's mandate and see every truth of the realm.

sentences.zh: 是以九域宅心，幽遐企踵，思佇雲羅，混網四裔。

translations.literal: Therefore the nine regions take you as heart; the distant crane their heels, thinking to wait under cloud nets and net the four frontiers in one mesh.
translations.idiomatic: The world waits for you to cast the net of restoration.

sentences.zh: 誠宜遠圖廟算，大存經略，光復舊京，疆理華夏，使惠風陽澤洽被八表，霜威寒飆陵振無外，豈不允應靈休，天人齊契！

translations.literal: Truly you should plan far in temple calculation, greatly preserve strategy, restore the old capital, order Huaxia within borders, let favoring wind and sunny moisture reach the eight outer regions, let frost awe and cold blast shake what lies beyond—is this not a fitting response to numinous blessing, heaven and man in accord!
translations.idiomatic: Move the capital north, rule all under heaven—heaven wills it.

sentences.zh: 今江河悠闊，風馬殊邈，故向義之徒履亡相尋，而建節之士猶繼踵無悔。

translations.literal: Now the Yangtze and Han are wide; wind and horse are far apart—therefore those who turned to righteousness tread ruin one after another, yet men who raise the credential still follow without regret.
translations.idiomatic: The river still divides north and south, yet volunteers keep coming.

sentences.zh: 況辰極既回，眾星斯仰，本源既運，枝泒自遷；

translations.literal: Moreover once the pole star has turned, all stars look up to it; once the root source moves, branches and twigs naturally shift;
translations.idiomatic: When the center moves, the limbs follow.

sentences.zh: 則晉之余黎欣皇德之攸憑，群凶妖逆知滅亡之無日，騁思順之心，鼓雷霆之勢，則二豎之命不誅而自絕矣。

translations.literal: then Jin's surviving people will rejoice in the royal virtue they rely on; the crowd of vicious rebels will know their destruction has no day left; thoughts of submission will gallop, thunderbolt momentum will drum—and the two miscreants' fate will end without execution.
translations.idiomatic: The people will rally; the rebels will wither.

sentences.zh: 故員通貴於無滯，明哲尚于應機，砎如石焉，所以成務。

translations.literal: Therefore comprehensive penetration is prized in not sticking; wise clarity esteems meeting the moment—firm as stone, thereby completing the task.
translations.idiomatic: Flexibility and timing—not rigidity—win wars.

sentences.zh: 若乃海運既徒，而鵬翼不舉，永結根于南垂，廢神州于龍漠，令五尺之童掩口而歎息。

translations.literal: If the sea road is already shifted yet the roc's wings do not rise, forever rooting at the southern edge, abandoning the divine land to the dragon desert, you will make even a five-foot child cover his mouth and sigh.
translations.idiomatic: If the court stays south, children will groan at the lost north.

sentences.zh: :夫先王經始，玄聖宅心，畫為九州，制為九服，貴中區而內諸夏，誠以晷度自中，霜露惟均，冠冕萬國，朝宗四海故也。

translations.literal: "The former kings began the realm; the dark sages dwelt in mind; they drew the nine provinces, regulated the nine domains, honoring the central region and embracing the Xia within—truly because the sundial's measure is centered, frost and dew fall even, cap and crown the myriad states, and the four seas pay court.
translations.idiomatic: The sages built China around the Central Plain for good reason.

sentences.zh: 自強胡陵暴，中華蕩覆，狼狽失據，權幸揚越，蠖屈以待龍伸之會，潛蟠之俟風雲之期，蓋屯圮所鐘，非理勝而然也。

translations.literal: Since the mighty Hu tyrannized, Huaxia was overturned; we stumbled losing footing, by expediency took refuge south of the Yang, coiled to wait the dragon's stretch, lurked to await wind and cloud—this is what hard fate heaped, not reason conquering thus.
translations.idiomatic: We fled south under duress—not by choice.

sentences.zh: 而喪亂緬邈，五十餘載，先舊徂沒，後來童幼，班荊輟音，積習成俗，遂望絕於本邦，宴安於所托。

translations.literal: Yet turmoil stretches far—more than fifty years; the old are gone, the young who follow, laying brushwood and breaking voice, habit piled into custom, thus hope is cut off from the native land and ease rests in the place they lodged.
translations.idiomatic: Two generations have grown up south of the river and forgotten the north.

sentences.zh: 眷言悼之，不覺悲歎！

translations.literal: Speaking of it with fond grief, one cannot help sighing in sorrow!
translations.idiomatic: That thought breaks the heart.

sentences.zh: 臣雖庸劣，才不周務，然攝官承乏，屬當重任，願竭筋骨，宣力先鋒，翦除荊棘，驅諸豺狼。

translations.literal: Your subject, though mediocre and weak, talent not comprehensive in tasks, yet holding office in succession, has met a heavy charge—I wish to exhaust sinew and bone, exert strength in the vanguard, cut away brambles, drive off wolves.
translations.idiomatic: I am no genius, but I will clear the thorns myself.

sentences.zh: 自永嘉之亂，播流江表者，請一切北徙，以實河南，資其舊業，反其土宇，勸農桑之務，盡三時之利，導之以義，齊之以禮，使文武兼宣，信順交暢，井邑既修，綱維粗舉。

translations.literal: Those drifted to the river's south since the Yongjia turmoil—let all be moved north to fill Henan, supply their old estates, return them to native soil, urge farming and mulberry, exhaust the three seasons' profit, guide them with right principle, align them with ritual, let civil and military both be proclaimed, trust and compliance cross in brightness—then hamlets will be ordered and the net of rule roughly raised.
translations.idiomatic: Resettle every refugee from Yongjia back into Henan, rebuild farms, restore ritual—

sentences.zh: 然後陛下建三辰之章，振旂旗之旌，冕旒錫鑾，朝服濟江，則宇宙之內誰不幸甚！

translations.literal: then Your Majesty may raise the three-luminaries standard, shake the banner and pennant, crown-beads and bell-chariot, court dress cross the river—then within the universe who would not be supremely fortunate!"
translations.idiomatic: then you can ride north in full regalia and the world will cheer."

sentences.zh: :夫人情昧安，難與圖始；

translations.literal: "Human feeling is blind to ease—hard to plot beginnings with;
translations.idiomatic: People cling to comfort—

sentences.zh: 非常之事，眾人所疑。

translations.literal: extraordinary affairs are what the multitude doubts.
translations.idiomatic: great ventures breed doubt.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下決玄照之明，斷常均之外，責臣以興復之效，委臣以終濟之功。

translations.literal: I humbly beg Your Majesty to resolve with dark-mirror clarity, decide beyond the usual balance, charge your subject with the effect of restoration, entrust your subject with the deed of final salvation.
translations.idiomatic: See clearly, charge me with recovery, hold me to results.

sentences.zh: 此事既就，此功既成，則陛下盛勳比靈斯前代，周宣之詠復興當年。

translations.literal: When this affair is done and this merit completed, then Your Majesty's splendid merit will match numinous antiquity, and the ode to King Xuan's revival will belong to this year.
translations.idiomatic: Success will make you another King Xuan.

sentences.zh: 如其不效，臣之罪也，褰裳赴鑊，其甘如薺。

translations.literal: If it does not succeed, it is your subject's crime—I will tuck up skirt and go to the cauldron; its sweetness will be like shepherd's purse.
translations.idiomatic: If I fail, boil me alive—I accept it."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「在昔喪亂，忽涉五紀，戎狄肆暴，繼襲凶跡，眷言西顧，慨歎盈懷！

translations.literal: An edict said, "In the past in turmoil we suddenly crossed five cycles; the Rong and Di ran wild, inheriting vicious tracks; speaking with fond words westward, sighs fill the breast!
translations.idiomatic: The edict mourned fifty years of barbarian rule.

sentences.zh: 知欲躬率三軍，蕩滌氛穢，廓清中畿，光復舊京，非夫外身殉國，孰能若此者哉！

translations.literal: Knowing you wish personally to lead the three armies, wash away foul miasma, clear the central heartland, restore the old capital—unless one gives body for the state, who could do thus!"
translations.idiomatic: It praised Huan Wen's willingness to die for the north."

sentences.zh: 諸所處分，委之高算。

translations.literal: All dispositions are entrusted to your lofty calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Strategy is his.

sentences.zh: 但河洛丘墟，所營者廣，經始之勤，致勞懷也。

translations.literal: But He and Luo are mounds and ruins; what is to be built is vast—the toil of starting work will weary mind and heart.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang is rubble—the work will exhaust you."

sentences.zh: 」於是改授並、司、冀三州，以交廣遼遠，罷都督，溫表辭不受。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was reassigned Bing, Si, and Ji three provinces; because Jiao and Guang were distant, area command was ended; Wen memorialized declining and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was given Bing, Si, and Ji; Jiao-Guang command was stripped; he declined parts of the bundle.

sentences.zh: 又加侍中、大司馬、都督中外諸軍事、假黃鉞。

translations.literal: He was additionally given Palace Attendant, Grand Marshal, area commander for all military affairs within and without, and the yellow battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: They added grand marshal, palace attendant, and yellow axe.

sentences.zh: 溫以既總督內外，不宜在遠，又上疏陳便宜七事：其一，朋黨雷同，私議沸騰，宜抑杜浮競，莫使能植。

translations.literal: Wen, since he now commanded inside and outside, ought not be far away; he again submitted a memorial stating seven convenient measures: first, factions echo one another and private talk boils—you should check vain rivalry and not let it take root.
translations.idiomatic: He offered seven reforms: crush cliques,

sentences.zh: 其二，戶口凋寡，不當漢之一郡，宜並官省職，令久於其事。

translations.literal: second, household registers are withered and few, not matching one Han commandery—you should merge offices and cut posts, letting men long hold their tasks.
translations.idiomatic: merge offices for shrunken population,

sentences.zh: 其三，機務不可停廢，常行文案宜為限日。

translations.literal: third, critical business may not stop; routine paperwork should have fixed deadlines.
translations.idiomatic: deadlines on paperwork,

sentences.zh: 其四，宜明長幼之禮，獎忠公之吏。

translations.literal: fourth, you should clarify ritual of elder and younger and reward loyal, upright officials.
translations.idiomatic: honor age and loyalty,

sentences.zh: 其五，褒貶賞罰，宜允其實。

translations.literal: fifth, praise and blame, reward and punishment, should match the facts.
translations.idiomatic: fair justice,

sentences.zh: 其六，宜述遵前典，敦明學業。

translations.literal: sixth, you should follow former canons and encourage learning.
translations.idiomatic: promote schools,

sentences.zh: 其七，宜選建史官，以成晉書。

translations.literal: seventh, you should select and establish historiographers to complete the Jin book.
translations.idiomatic: and commission the *History of Jin*."

sentences.zh: 有司皆奏行之。

translations.literal: The bureaus all memorialized to implement them.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries adopted all seven.

sentences.zh: 尋加羽葆鼓吹，置左右長史、司馬、從事中郎四人。

translations.literal: Soon feather-canopy processional music was added, with four senior clerks, majors, and clerks each on left and right.
translations.idiomatic: He got the drum escort and a full staff.

sentences.zh: 受鼓吹，餘皆辭。

translations.literal: He accepted the processional music; the rest he declined.
translations.idiomatic: He took only the music.

sentences.zh: 復率舟軍進合肥。

translations.literal: Again he led the fleet to advance on Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: He sailed against Hefei again.

sentences.zh: 加揚州牧、錄尚書事，使侍中顏旄宣旨，召溫入參朝政。

translations.literal: He was given Governor of Yang Province and Recorder of the Masters of Writing; Palace Attendant Yan Mao was sent to proclaim the edict summoning Wen to join court governance.
translations.idiomatic: They made him recorder and Yang governor and summoned him to court.

sentences.zh: 溫上疏曰：

translations.literal: Wen submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: He answered:

sentences.zh: :方攘除群凶，掃平禍亂，當竭天下智力，與眾共濟，而朝議咸疑，聖詔彌固，事異本圖，豈敢執遂！

translations.literal: "Just now sweeping away the flock of villains and leveling disaster and chaos ought to exhaust the realm's wisdom and strength and aid the multitude together—yet court discussion all hesitates, the sage edict ever firmer; the affair differs from the original plan—how dare I insist!
translations.idiomatic: I mean to finish the bandits first—the summons to court is premature."

sentences.zh: 至於入參朝政，非所敢聞。

translations.literal: As for entering to join court governance—that is not what I dare hear.
translations.idiomatic: He refused a desk in the capital.

sentences.zh: 臣違離宮省二十餘載，鞸䩬戎務，役勤思苦，若得解帶逍遙，鳴玉闕廷，參贊無為之契，豫聞曲成之化，雖實不敏，豈不是願！

translations.literal: Your subject has been apart from palace and ministries over twenty years, girded in military affairs, toiled in duty with bitter thought—if I could loosen belt and roam free, jade-tinkle in the palace court, join in assisting the tally of non-action, share in hearing the transforming power of thorough completion—though truly not keen, how could it not be my wish!
translations.idiomatic: Part of him longed for capital life—

sentences.zh: 但顧以江漢艱難，不同曩日，而益梁新平，寧州始服，懸兵漢川，戍禦彌廣，加強蠻盤牙，勢處上流，江湖悠遠，當制命侯伯，自非望實重威，無以鎮禦遐外。

translations.literal: but considering the hardship of Jiang and Han is not as in former days, while Yi and Liang are newly pacified and Ningzhou first submits, troops hang over the Han plain, garrison defense grows broader, and strong Man interlock like teeth in a situation on the upper reaches—rivers and lakes stretch far; one must command the border lords—unless reputation and substance weigh heavy with awe, there is no way to guard the distant marches.
translations.idiomatic: but the upper Yangzi still needs a strong hand.

sentences.zh: 臣知舍此之艱危，敢背之而無怨，願奮臂投身造事中原者，實恥帝道皇居仄陋于東南，痛神華桑梓遂埋于戎狄。

translations.literal: Your subject knows the peril of abandoning this—dares turn his back on it without resentment; the reason I wish to strain arms and throw body into making trouble in the central plain is truly that I am ashamed the imperial way and royal dwelling are cramped in the southeast, pained that divine Huaxia and native mulberry are buried under Rong and Di.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed to hold the west and finish the reconquest.

sentences.zh: 若憑宗廟之靈，則雲徹席捲，呼吸蕩清。

translations.literal: If we rely on the altars' numinous power, then clouds will roll up and mats sweep, in a breath all is swept clean.
translations.idiomatic: With ancestral help the north will clear in one gust.

sentences.zh: 如當假息遊魂，則臣據河洛，親臨二寇，廣宣皇靈，襟帶秦趙，遠不五載，大事必定。

translations.literal: If they should borrow breath like roaming souls, then your subject will hold He and Luo in person, face the two foes, broadly proclaim royal numen, girdle Qin and Zhao—far off, within five years, the great affair is sure to be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Else he would anchor at Luoyang and grind Qin and Zhao down within five years."

sentences.zh: :今臣昱以親賢贊國，光輔二世，即無煩以臣疏鈍，並是機務。

translations.literal: "Now your subject Yu, as kin and worthy, aids the state and brilliantly assists two reigns—there is then no need to burden the court with your subject's dullness in all the machinery of state.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yu can run the capital without me.

sentences.zh: 且不有行者，誰捍牧圉？

translations.literal: Moreover without a man in the field, who defends the pastures?
translations.idiomatic: Someone must hold the frontier.

sentences.zh: 表裏相濟，實深實重。

translations.literal: Outside and inside aiding each other is truly deep and truly weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Court and camp need each other.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下察臣所陳，兼訪內外，乞時還屯，撫甯方隅。

translations.literal: I humbly beg Your Majesty examine what your subject has opened, also inquire within and without; I beg timely return to garrison and pacify the regions.
translations.idiomatic: Let me return to my post and steady the west."

sentences.zh: 詔不許，復征溫。

translations.literal: An edict did not permit; again he summoned Wen.
translations.idiomatic: The throne refused and recalled him again.

sentences.zh: 溫至赭圻，詔又使尚書車灌止之，溫遂城赭圻，固讓內錄，遙領揚州牧。

translations.literal: When Wen reached Zheqi, an edict again ordered Minister of the Masters of Writing Che Guan to stop him; Wen thereupon walled Zheqi, firmly declined inner recorder, and held Yang governor at long distance.
translations.idiomatic: At Zheqi he fortified, refused the recorder post, kept Yangzhou in name only.

sentences.zh: 屬鮮卑攻洛陽，陳祐出奔，簡文帝時輔政，會溫於洌洲，議征討事，溫移鎮姑孰。

translations.literal: It happened that Xianbei attacked Luoyang; Chen You fled; Prince Jianwen then assisted governance and met Wen on Lie Isle to deliberate campaigning; Wen moved headquarters to Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: Xianbei hit Luoyang; Sima Yu met Huan Wen on the river; Huan Wen moved to Gushu.

sentences.zh: 會哀帝崩，事遂寢。

translations.literal: It happened that Emperor Ai died; the affair then slept.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai died and the campaign stalled.

sentences.zh: 溫性儉，每燕惟下七奠柈茶果而已。

translations.literal: Wen by nature was frugal; at each banquet he set out only seven trays of tea and fruit.
translations.idiomatic: His feasts were spare—tea and fruit on seven plates.

sentences.zh: 然以雄武專朝，窺覦非望，或臥對親僚曰：「為爾寂寂，將為文景所笑。

translations.literal: Yet with martial heroism monopolizing the court, he eyed illegitimate hope; sometimes lying down he told close staff, "If we stay this quiet, Emperors Wen and Jing will laugh at us."
translations.idiomatic: Privately he said quiet obscurity would make Han Wendi mock him.

sentences.zh: 」眾莫敢對。

translations.literal: " The crowd none dared answer.
translations.idiomatic: No one replied.

sentences.zh: 既而撫枕起曰：「既不能流芳後世，不足復遺臭萬載邪！

translations.literal: Then he slapped the pillow and rose, saying, "If we cannot leave fragrance for later ages, is it not still worth leaving a stench for ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: He added that infamy beat oblivion.

sentences.zh: 」嘗行經王敦墓，望之曰：「可人，可人！

translations.literal: " Once passing Wang Dun's tomb, he looked toward it and said, "A capable man, a capable man!"
translations.idiomatic: He praised Wang Dun's tomb.

sentences.zh: 」其心跡若是。

translations.literal: " His heart and tracks were thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his ambition.

sentences.zh: 時有遠方比丘尼名有道術，於別室浴，溫竊窺之。

translations.literal: At the time there was a nun from afar said to have arts; bathing in a separate room, Wen secretly peeped.
translations.idiomatic: He spied on a nun who claimed magic powers.

sentences.zh: 尼倮身先以刀自破腹，次斷兩足。

translations.literal: The nun stripped naked and first with a knife cut open her own belly, then severed both feet.
translations.idiomatic: The nun disemboweled herself and hacked off her own feet before answering.

sentences.zh: 浴竟出，溫問吉凶，尼云：「公若作天子，亦當如是。」

translations.literal: When the bath was finished and she came out, Wen asked good or ill fortune; the nun said, "If my lord becomes Son of Heaven, it will also be thus."
translations.idiomatic: Afterward she told him an emperor's fate looked like her self-mutilation.

sentences.zh: ，又上疏悉眾北伐。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial mustering the full host for a northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The line opens with a stray comma in the edition; he again demanded a full northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 平北將軍郗愔以疾解職，又以溫領平北將軍、徐兗二州刺史，率弟南中郎沖、西中郎袁真步騎五萬北伐。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the North Chi Yin resigned due to illness; Wen was additionally given General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Xu and Yan provinces; he led his younger brother, General of the Center of the South Chong, and General of the Center of the West Yuan Zhen with fifty thousand foot and horse on the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Yin stepped down; Huan Wen took Xu-Yan command and marched fifty thousand with Huan Chong and Yuan Zhen.

sentences.zh: 百官皆于南州祖道，都邑盡傾。

translations.literal: The hundred officials all saw him off with roadside libations at South Prefecture; the capital turned out entirely.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court lined Nanzhou to toast the army.

sentences.zh: 軍次湖陸，攻慕容暐將慕容忠，獲之，進次金鄉。

translations.literal: The army halted at Hulu, attacked Murong Wei's general Murong Zhong, captured him, and advanced to station at Jinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He took Murong Zhong at Hulu and pushed to Jinxiang.

sentences.zh: 時亢旱，水道不通，乃鑿钜野三百餘里以通舟運，自清水入河。

translations.literal: At the time drought was extreme and waterways did not connect; he therefore dug through Juye over three hundred li to open boat transport, entering the Yellow River from Clear Water.
translations.idiomatic: He cut a canal through Juye to link the rivers in a drought.

sentences.zh: 暐將慕容垂、傅末波等率眾八萬距溫，戰于林渚。

translations.literal: Wei's generals Murong Chui, Fu Mobo, and others led eighty thousand to oppose Wen and fought at Linzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui met him with eighty thousand at Linzhu.

sentences.zh: 溫擊破之，遂至枋頭。

translations.literal: Wen broke them and reached Fangtou.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen fought through to Fangtou.

sentences.zh: 先使袁真伐譙梁，開石門以通運。

translations.literal: He first sent Yuan Zhen to campaign against Qiao and Liang and open Stone Gate for transport.
