translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen was to open the Stone Gate supply line.

sentences.zh: 真討譙梁皆平之，而不能開石門，軍糧竭盡。

translations.literal: Zhen campaigned against Qiao and Liang and pacified both, but could not open Stone Gate; army grain was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen cleared Qiao-Liang but never opened Stone Gate—supplies died.

sentences.zh: 溫焚舟步退，自東燕出倉垣，經陳留，鑿井而飲，行七百餘里。

translations.literal: Wen burned boats and withdrew on foot, came out from Dongyan through Cangyuan, passed Chenliu, dug wells for water, and marched more than seven hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen scuttled his fleet and marched seven hundred li of dry country.

sentences.zh: 垂以八千騎追之，戰於襄邑，溫軍敗績，死者三萬人。

translations.literal: Chui with eight thousand horse pursued him; they fought at Xiangyi; Wen's army was routed; dead numbered thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui ran him down at Xiangyi—thirty thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 溫甚恥之，歸罪於真，表廢為庶人。

translations.literal: Wen was deeply shamed, blamed Zhen, and memorialized to degrade him to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: He scapegoated Yuan Zhen and stripped his rank.

sentences.zh: 真怨溫誣己，據壽陽以自固，潛通苻堅、慕容暐。

translations.literal: Zhen resented Wen's slander, held Shouyang to secure himself, and secretly communicated with Fu Jian and Murong Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen rebelled at Shouyang and wrote to Fu Jian and Murong Wei.

sentences.zh: 帝遣侍中羅含以牛酒犒溫于山陽，使會稽王昱會溫於途中，詔以溫世子給事熙為征虜將軍、豫州刺史、假節。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Palace Attendant Luo Han with cattle and wine to console Wen at Shanyang, had Prince of Kuaiji Yu meet Wen on the road, and issued an edict making Wen's heir, Attendant Xi, General Who Conquers the Caitiffs, Governor of Yu Province, and invested with the staff of authority.
translations.idiomatic: The court soothed Huan Wen en route and named his son Huan Xi governor of Yu.

sentences.zh: 及南康公主薨，詔賻布千匹，錢百萬，溫辭不受。

translations.literal: When Princess of Nankang died, an edict granted a thousand bolts of cloth for funeral expenses and a million cash; Wen declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the princess's funeral subsidy.

sentences.zh: 又陳息熙三年之孤，且年少未宜使居偏任，詔不許。

translations.literal: He also stated that his son Xi was a three-year orphan and moreover young and not yet fit to hold a side appointment; an edict did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: He begged off Huan Xi's post as too young; the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 發州人築廣陵城，移鎮之。

translations.literal: He drafted the province's people to build Guangling walls and moved his headquarters there.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted labor for Guangling's walls and shifted his base.

sentences.zh: 時溫行役既久，又兼疾癘，死者十四五，百姓嗟怨。

translations.literal: At the time Wen's campaigns had already been long, and pestilence joined them; dead were four or five in ten; the hundred surnames groaned in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Disease and fatigue killed nearly half his levies; people cursed him.

sentences.zh: 袁真病死，其將朱輔立其子瑾以嗣事。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhen died of illness; his officer Zhu Fu set up Zhen's son Jin to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen died; Zhu Fu raised Yuan Jin.

sentences.zh: 慕容暐、苻堅並遣軍授瑾，溫使督護竺瑤、矯陽之等與水軍擊之。

translations.literal: Murong Wei and Fu Jian both sent troops to aid Jin; Wen sent Protector Zhu Yao, Jiao Yangzhi, and others with the naval force to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Former Yan and Former Qin reinforced Shouyang; Huan Wen sent Zhu Yao and allies by water.

sentences.zh: 時暐軍已至，瑤等與戰于武丘，破之。

translations.literal: At the time Wei's army had already arrived; Yao and others fought them at Wuqiu and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yao beat the Yan column at Wuqiu.

sentences.zh: 溫率二萬人自廣陵又至，瑾嬰城固守，溫築長圍守之。

translations.literal: Wen led twenty thousand from Guangling and arrived again; Jin held the city with ringed defense; Wen built long siegeworks to contain him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen ringed Shouyang with twenty thousand fresh troops.

sentences.zh: 苻堅乃使其將王鑒、張蠔等率兵以救瑾，屯洛澗，先遣精騎五千次於肥水北。

translations.literal: Fu Jian then sent his generals Wang Jian and Zhang Hao and others to lead troops to rescue Jin, camping at Luojian; he first sent five thousand picked horse to station north of the Fei River.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian sent Wang Jian and Zhang Hao toward the Fei.

sentences.zh: 溫遣桓伊及弟子石虔等逆擊，大破之，瑾眾遂潰，生擒之，並其宗族數十人及硃輔送於京都而斬之，所侍養乞活數百人悉坑之，以妻子為賞。

translations.literal: Wen sent Huan Yi and his nephew Shi Qian and others to meet and strike them, greatly defeating them; Jin's host then collapsed; he was taken alive, together with several tens of his clan and Zhu Fu, sent to the capital and executed; several hundred "living-for-bread" dependents they had maintained were all buried alive; wives and children were given as rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yi shattered the Qin relief force, took Yuan Jin alive, executed his clan, buried hundreds of followers alive, and parceled out families as booty.

sentences.zh: 溫以功，詔加班劍十人，犒軍于路次，文武論功賞賜各有差。

translations.literal: For the merit an edict added ten patterned-sword guards, feasted the army by the roadside, and civil and military were graded for reward.
translations.idiomatic: The court added honors and paid bonuses by rank.

sentences.zh: 溫既負其才力，久懷異志，欲先立功河朔，還受九錫。

translations.literal: Wen, bearing his talent and force, long harbored a different aim, wishing first to win merit north of the Yellow River, then receive the nine bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to conquer the north, then take the nine imperial gifts.

sentences.zh: 既逢覆敗，名實頓減，於是參軍郗超進廢立之計，溫乃廢帝而立簡文帝。

translations.literal: Having met crushing defeat, name and substance suddenly shrank; thereupon his clerk Chi Chao advanced a plan to depose and establish; Wen then deposed the Emperor and set up Emperor Jianwen.
translations.idiomatic: After Fangtou, Chi Chao talked him into a coup—he deposed Emperor Fei and enthroned Sima Yu.

sentences.zh: 詔溫依諸葛亮故事，甲仗百人入殿，賜錢五千萬，絹二萬匹，布十萬匹。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Wen to follow Zhuge Liang's precedent, one hundred armored attendants in the hall, and granted fifty million cash, twenty thousand bolts of silk, and one hundred thousand bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: He was allowed a hundred guards in the hall like Zhuge Liang, plus a huge cash and silk gift.

sentences.zh: 溫多所廢徒，誅庾倩、殷涓、曹秀等。

translations.literal: Wen dismissed and banished many, executing Yu Qian, Yin Juan, Cao Xiu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He purged Yu Qian, Yin Juan, Cao Xiu, and more.

sentences.zh: 是時溫威勢翕赫，侍中謝安見而遙拜，溫驚曰：「安石，卿何事乃爾！

translations.literal: At the time Wen's awe-striking power blazed; Palace Attendant Xie An saw him and bowed from afar; Wen startled said, "Anshi, why do you do this!"
translations.idiomatic: Xie An bowed from a distance; Huan Wen demanded why.

sentences.zh: 」安曰：「未有君拜於前，臣揖於後。

translations.literal: " An said, "Never has the lord bowed in front while the minister only cupped hands behind."
translations.idiomatic: Xie An said no king bows while a minister merely inclines his head.

sentences.zh: 」時溫有腳疾，詔乘輿入朝，既見，欲陳廢立本意，帝便泣下數十行，溫兢懼，不得一言而出。

translations.literal: " At the time Wen had foot ailment; an edict ordered him to ride the imperial palanquin into court; once he saw him, he wished to state the original intent of depose-and-establish; the Emperor then wept several tens of lines; Wen trembled in fear and could not speak a word before leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen rode to court but Sima Yu's tears silenced him.

sentences.zh: 初，元明世，郭璞為讖曰：「君非無嗣，兄弟代禪。

translations.literal: At first, in the eras of Yuan and Ming, Guo Pu made a prophecy, saying, "The lord is not without heir—brothers will pass the throne in turn."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu's prophecy spoke of brotherly succession.

sentences.zh: 」謂成帝有子，而以國祚傳弟。

translations.literal: " It meant Emperor Cheng had a son yet the mandate passed to a younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: It referred to Cheng's line passing sideways.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「有人姓李，兒專征戰。

translations.literal: It also said, "There will be one surnamed Li whose 'child' specializes in war campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Another line named a Li and a "child" of war.

sentences.zh: 譬如車軸，脫在一面。

translations.literal: "Like a cart axle, the pin slips to one side."
translations.idiomatic: Like a loose axle pin.

sentences.zh: 」兒者，子也；

translations.literal: "The word read as 'child' in the verse means 'son';
translations.idiomatic: The prophecy glosses the character for 'child' as the word for son.

sentences.zh: 李去子木存，車去軸為亙，合成「桓」字也。

translations.literal: remove 'zi' from Li and 'mu' remains; remove 'che' and 'zhou' from cart-axle and 'heng' remains—together they form the character 'Huan.'"
translations.idiomatic: The riddle's pieces spell the surname Huan.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「爾來，爾來，河內大縣。

translations.literal: It also said, "Er lai, er lai—a great county in Henei."
translations.idiomatic: Another verse played on "er lai" and Henei.

sentences.zh: 」爾來謂自爾已來為元始，溫字元子也；

translations.literal: " 'Er lai' means "from then on" as a beginning—Wen's style is Yuanzi;
translations.idiomatic: Er lai punned on Huan Wen's courtesy name Yuanzi.

sentences.zh: 故河內大縣，溫也。

translations.literal: therefore the great county in Henei is Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Henei stood for Huan Wen.

sentences.zh: 成康既崩，桓氏始大，故連言之。

translations.literal: After Cheng and Kang passed away, the Huan clan first grew great—therefore it is strung together in one saying.
translations.idiomatic: The verses foretold Huan power after Cheng and Kang.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「賴子之薨，延我國祚。

translations.literal: It also said, "Thanks to the heir's death, our state's mandate is prolonged.
translations.idiomatic: One line blessed an heir's death as prolonging Jin.

sentences.zh: 痛子之隕，皇運其暮。

translations.literal: Grief for the heir's fall—the royal fortune reaches evening."
translations.idiomatic: Another mourned an heir and twilight of the house.

sentences.zh: 」二子者，元子、道子也。

translations.literal: " The two sons mean Yuanzi and Daozi.
translations.idiomatic: The two sons were Huan Wen and Sima Daozi.

sentences.zh: 溫志在篡奪，事未成而死，幸之也。

translations.literal: Wen's aim was usurpation; the affair did not succeed and he died—fortunate indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen died before stealing the throne—mercy for Jin.

sentences.zh: 會稽王道子雖首亂晉國，而其死亦晉衰之由也，故云痛也。

translations.literal: Prince Kuaiji Daozi though first threw Jin into turmoil, yet his death too was a reason for Jin's decline—therefore it says "grief."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Daozi later ruined the state—hence the prophecy's "grief."

sentences.zh: 溫復還白石，上疏求歸姑孰。

translations.literal: Wen returned again to Baishi and submitted a memorial begging to return to Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to Baishi and asked to go back to Gushu.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「夫乾坤體合，而化成萬物；

translations.literal: An edict said, "As for Qian and Kun's bodies joining and transforming the myriad things;
translations.idiomatic: The edict quoted the classics: heaven and earth unite—

sentences.zh: 二人同心，則不言所利。

translations.literal: when two men share one heart, they need not speak of profit."
translations.idiomatic: two hearts as one need no words of gain."

sentences.zh: 古之哲王咸賴元輔，姬旦光於四表，而周道以隆；

translations.literal: The sage kings of old all relied on their chief ministers; the Duke of Zhou shone to the four borders and the Zhou way thereby rose;
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou lit the realm—

sentences.zh: 伊尹格於皇天，而殷化以洽。

translations.literal: Yi Yin reached to August Heaven and Yin transformation was harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Yin perfected Shang rule—

sentences.zh: 大司馬明德應期，光大深遠，上合天心，含章時發，用集大命，在予一人，功美博陸，道固萬世。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal's bright virtue answers the season, his greatness and depth far-reaching, above joining heaven's mind, holding pattern and manifesting in season—thereby the great mandate gathers on Us alone; his merit matches Bo Lu, his way is firm for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: It hailed Huan Wen as Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 今進公丞相，其大司馬本官皆如故，留公京都，以鎮社稷。

translations.literal: Now We advance the duke to Chancellor; his Grand Marshal original posts all remain as before; retain the duke in the capital to anchor the altars."
translations.idiomatic: It offered him the chancellorship and a capital post."

sentences.zh: 」溫固辭，仍請還鎮。

translations.literal: " Wen firmly declined and still begged to return to garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen refused the capital job.

sentences.zh: 遣侍中王坦之徵溫入相，增邑為萬戶，又辭。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Wang Tanzhi was sent to summon Wen to be chancellor; his fief was increased to ten thousand households; again he declined.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tanzhi tried to drag him to chancellor—still no.

sentences.zh: 詔以西府經袁真事故，軍用不足，給世子熙布三萬匹，米六萬斛，又以熙弟濟為給事中。

translations.literal: An edict said that because the western bureau had passed through Yuan Zhen's affair, military supplies were insufficient; three ten thousand bolts of cloth and sixty thousand hu of grain were given to heir Xi, and Xi's younger brother Ji was made Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The court subsidized his heir with grain and cloth after Yuan Zhen's war costs.

sentences.zh: 及帝不豫，詔溫曰：「吾遂委篤，足下便入，冀得相見。

translations.literal: When the Emperor grew gravely ill, an edict told Wen, "We have sunk into critical illness; you should enter at once—we hope to see each other.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yu begged Huan Wen to his deathbed.

sentences.zh: 便來，便來！

translations.literal: Come, come!"
translations.idiomatic: Come at once!"

sentences.zh: 」於是一日一夜頻有四詔。

translations.literal: " Thereupon in one day and night edicts came four times in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Four summons flew in one night.

sentences.zh: 溫上疏曰：「聖體不和，以經積日，愚心惶恐，無所寄情。

translations.literal: Wen submitted a memorial saying, "The sage person is unwell and has been so for accumulated days; foolish heart is fearful and anxious, with nowhere to lodge feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen offered a careful reply about succession.

sentences.zh: 夫盛衰常理，過備無害，故漢高枕疾，呂後問相，孝武不豫，霍光啟嗣。

translations.literal: Rise and fall are constant principle; excess preparation does no harm—therefore Gaozu of Han lay ill and Empress Lü asked about the minister; Emperor Wu of Han was unwell and Huo Guang opened the matter of the heir.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Han precedents for regency talks.

sentences.zh: 嗚噎以問身後，蓋所存者大也。

translations.literal: Choking, they asked about after the body—what they stored was the great matter.
translations.idiomatic: They planned for the realm, not themselves.

sentences.zh: 今皇子幼稚，而朝賢時譽惟謝安、王坦之才識智皆簡在聖鑒。

translations.literal: Now the imperial sons are young, yet among court worthies the timely praise is only for Xie An and Wang Tanzhi—talent and judgment are both briefly within sage mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Name Xie An and Wang Tanzhi for the boy.

sentences.zh: 內輔幼君，外禦強寇，實群情之大懼，然理盡於此。

translations.literal: Within, assist the young lord; without, ward the strong foe—truly it is the multitude's great fear, yet principle exhausts here.
translations.idiomatic: They must guard within and without—that is the limit of the plan.

sentences.zh: 陛下便宜崇授，使群下知所寄，而安等奉命陳力，公私為宜。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should then loftily invest them, letting subordinates know where trust rests; then An and the rest may receive orders and exert strength—fitting for public and private.
translations.idiomatic: Empower them openly so the court knows who rules.

sentences.zh: 至如臣溫位兼將相，加陛下垂布衣之顧，但朽邁疾病，懼不支久，無所復堪托以後事。

translations.literal: As for your subject Wen, rank combines general and minister, plus Your Majesty's favor of common-cloth regard—but I am rotten with age and disease, fear I cannot last long, and have nothing further to entrust for after affairs."
translations.idiomatic: He excused himself as too old to regent."

sentences.zh: 」疏未及奏而帝崩，遺詔家國事一稟之於公，如諸葛武侯、王丞相故事。

translations.literal: " Before the memorial could be presented the Emperor died; the death edict handed state and house affairs entirely to the duke, following the precedents of Martial Marquis Zhuge and Chancellor Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yu died; the will made Huan Wen regent like Zhuge Liang and Wang Dao.

sentences.zh: 溫初望簡文臨終禪位於己，不爾便為周公居攝。

translations.literal: Wen at first hoped Jianwen on dying would yield the throne to himself; if not that, then be Duke of Zhou holding the regency.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen expected abdication or a Zhou-gong regency.

sentences.zh: 事既不副所望，故甚憤怨，與弟沖書曰：「遺詔使吾依武侯、王公故事耳。

translations.literal: The affair did not match what he hoped for; therefore he was very resentful and angry; he wrote his brother Chong, saying, "The death edict only tells me to follow Martial Marquis Wang and Duke Wang's stories."
translations.idiomatic: He raged to Huan Chong that the will snubbed him.

sentences.zh: 」王、謝處大事之際，日憤憤少懷。

translations.literal: " Wang and Xie, when the great matter hung, daily nursed sullen, small-minded thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: He cursed Wang Dao's heirs and Xie for blocking him.

sentences.zh: 及孝武即位，詔曰：「先帝遺敕云：'事大司馬如事吾。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended, an edict said, "The late Emperor's dying instruction said: 'Serve the Grand Marshal as you would serve Us.'"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu's edict quoted fealty to Huan Wen.

sentences.zh: '令答表便可盡敬。

translations.literal: "Order that answering memorials may show full respect."
translations.idiomatic: Memorials to him should use full ritual."

sentences.zh: 」又詔：「大司馬社稷所寄，先帝托以家國，內外眾事便就關公施行。

translations.literal: " Another edict: "The Grand Marshal is what the altars lean on; the late Emperor entrusted him with house and state—all matters within and without may be referred to the duke for execution."
translations.idiomatic: A second edict gave him total executive power.

sentences.zh: 」復遣謝安徵溫入輔，加前部羽葆鼓吹，武賁六十人，溫讓不受。

translations.literal: " Again Xie An was sent to summon Wen to assist governance, adding front escort feather-canopy music and sixty household guards; Wen declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An summoned him to court with full pomp; he refused.

sentences.zh: 及溫入朝，赴山陵，詔曰：「公勳德尊重，師保朕躬，兼有風患，其無敬。

translations.literal: When Wen entered court for the imperial tomb, an edict said, "The duke's merit and virtue are weighty; you tutor Our person; you also have wind ailment—need not show full deference."
translations.idiomatic: He was excused full bows because of gout.

sentences.zh: 」又敕尚書安等於新亭奉迎，百僚皆拜於道側。

translations.literal: " Another order commanded An and the others to welcome him at Xinting; the hundred officials all bowed by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: The court welcomed him at Xinting with full obeisance.

sentences.zh: 當時豫有位望者咸戰懾失色，或云因此殺王、謝，內外懷懼。

translations.literal: At the time all who held rank and standing in Yu trembled and lost color; some said he would on this occasion kill Wang and Xie; inside and outside nursed fear.
translations.idiomatic: Jiankang feared a blood purge of Wang and Xie.

sentences.zh: 溫既至，以盧悚入宮，乃收尚書陸始付廷尉，責替慢罪也。

translations.literal: Once Wen arrived, because Lu Song had entered the palace, he seized Masters of Writing Lu Shi and handed him to the tribunal, blaming negligence in the crime.
translations.idiomatic: He jailed Minister Lu Shi over Lu Song's intrusion.

sentences.zh: 於是拜高平陵，左右覺其有異，既登車，謂從者曰：「先帝向遂靈見。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bowed at Gaoping Tomb; attendants sensed something strange; once he boarded the carriage he told followers, "The late Emperor just now manifestly appeared to my spirit."
translations.idiomatic: At Gaoling he claimed a vision of Sima Yu.

sentences.zh: 」既不述帝所言，故眾莫之知，但見將拜時頻言「臣不敢」而已。

translations.literal: " He did not relate what the Emperor said, so the crowd knew nothing—only they saw that as he was about to bow he repeatedly said, "Your subject dares not."
translations.idiomatic: Witnesses heard only him muttering he dared not.

sentences.zh: 又問左右殷涓形狀，答者言肥短，溫云：「向亦見在帝側。

translations.literal: He again asked attendants Yin Juan's appearance; those who answered said short and stout; Wen said, "A moment ago I also saw him at the Emperor's side."
translations.idiomatic: He hallucinated Yin Juan beside the ghost emperor.

sentences.zh: 」初，殷浩既為溫所廢死，涓頗有氣尚，遂不詣溫，而與武陵王晞游，故溫疑而害之，竟不識也。

translations.literal: " At first, after Yin Hao had been deposed and killed by Wen, Juan had spirit and pride; he would not visit Wen but associated with Prince of Wuling Xi—therefore Wen suspected and harmed him, yet never actually met him.
translations.idiomatic: He had murdered Yin Juan without ever seeing him—guilt fed the vision.

sentences.zh: 及是，亦見涓為祟，因而遇疾。

translations.literal: When this happened, he also saw Juan as a haunting and on that account fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: The apparition broke his health.

sentences.zh: 凡停京師十有四日，歸於姑孰，遂寢疾不起。

translations.literal: In all he stopped at the capital fourteen days, returned to Gushu, and then lay ill and did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: After two weeks in the capital he fled to Gushu and collapsed.

sentences.zh: 諷朝廷加己九錫，累相催促。

translations.literal: He hinted to the court to add the nine bestowals to himself; repeatedly he pressed and hurried.
translations.idiomatic: He demanded the nine gifts while dying.

sentences.zh: 謝安、王坦之聞其病篤，密緩其事。

translations.literal: Xie An and Wang Tanzhi heard his illness was critical and secretly slowed the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An and Wang Tanzhi stalled the patent.

sentences.zh: 錫文未及成而薨，時年六十二。

translations.literal: The patent text had not been completed when he died, aged sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-two before the nine tins were sealed.

sentences.zh: 皇太后與帝臨於朝堂三日，詔賜九命袞冕之服，又朝服一具，衣一襲，東園秘器，錢二百萬，布二千匹，臘五百斤，以供喪事。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager and the Emperor mourned at the court hall three days; an edict granted nine-rank mourning robe and cap, another full court suit, one full change of clothes, eastern-park secret coffin gear, two million cash, two thousand bolts of cloth, and five hundred jin of cured meat to supply the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Court mourned three days and sent imperial-class burial goods.

sentences.zh: 及葬，一依太宰安平獻王、漢大將軍霍光故事，賜九旒鸞輅，黃屋左纛，縕輬車，輓歌二部，羽葆鼓吹，武賁班劍百人，優冊即前南郡公增七千五百戶，進地方三百里，賜錢五千萬，絹二萬匹，布十萬匹，追贈丞相。

translations.literal: At burial everything followed the precedents of Grand Preceptor Prince Xian of Anping and Grand General Huo Guang of Han—nine-bannered phoenix chariot, yellow canopy left streamer, enclosed hearse, two choirs of dirge, feather-canopy processional music, one hundred patterned-sword household guards; a splendid patent advanced the former Duke of Nan by seven thousand five hundred households, territory three hundred li square, fifty million cash, twenty thousand silk, one hundred thousand cloth, posthumous gift of Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Burial followed the full Huo Guang precedent: nine-plume phoenix hearse, imperial yellow canopy, wax-sealed coffin cart, two choirs of dirge, drum escort, a hundred sword guards, his dukedom enlarged by seventy-five hundred households over three hundred square li, millions in cash and silk, and posthumous appointment as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 初，沖問溫以謝安、王坦之所任，溫曰：「伊等不為汝所處分。

translations.literal: At first Chong asked Wen what he made of Xie An and Wang Tanzhi's appointments; Wen said, "They will not be subject to your disposal."
translations.idiomatic: He warned Huan Chong he could not control Xie An and Wang Tanzhi.

sentences.zh: 」溫知己存彼不敢異，害之無益於沖，更失時望，所以息謀。

translations.literal: " Wen knew that while he lived they dared not diverge; killing them would not benefit Chong and would further lose timely reputation—therefore he dropped the plot.
translations.idiomatic: While Huan Wen lived, Xie and Wang obeyed; killing them would have ruined Huan Chong's reputation, so he dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 溫六子：熙、濟、歆、禕、偉、玄。

translations.literal: Wen had six sons: Xi, Ji, Xin, Yi, Wei, and Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen fathered six sons.

sentences.zh: 熙字伯道，初為世子，後以才弱，使沖領其眾。

translations.literal: Xi, styled Bodao, was first heir; later because talent was weak, he had Chong lead his host.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xi lost the army to Huan Chong as untalented.

sentences.zh: 及溫病，熙與叔秘謀殺沖，沖知之，徙于長沙。

translations.literal: When Wen fell ill, Xi plotted with uncle Mi to kill Chong; Chong learned of it and banished him to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xi and Huan Mi plotted regicide; Huan Chong sent Xi to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 濟字仲道，與熙同謀，俱徙長沙。

translations.literal: Ji, styled Zhongdao, joined Xi in the plot; both were banished to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Ji shared the exile.

sentences.zh: 歆字叔道，賜爵臨賀公。

translations.literal: Xin, styled Shudao, was enfeoffed Duke of Linhe.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xin became duke of Linhe.

sentences.zh: 禕最愚，不辨菽麥。

translations.literal: Yi was the most foolish—he could not tell beans from wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yi was a simpleton who could not tell grain apart.

sentences.zh: 偉字幼道，平厚篤實，居籓為士庶所懷。

translations.literal: Wei, styled Youdao, was even, thick, and solid; holding a screen he was cherished by gentry and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wei was steady and beloved as a frontier lord.

sentences.zh: 曆使持節、督荊益甯秦梁五州諸軍事、安西將軍、領南蠻校尉、荊州刺史、西昌侯，贈驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He successively held credential-bearing office, area commander for Jing, Yi, Ning, Qin, and Liang five provinces' military affairs, General Who Pacifies the West, concurrent chief of the southern Man, Governor of Jing Province, Marquis of Xichang; posthumously gifted Grand General of Agile Cavalry with office equal to the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to western command over five provinces and died a grand general.

sentences.zh: 玄嗣爵，別有傳。

translations.literal: Xuan inherited the noble rank; he has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan has his own chapter.

translations.literal: The edition inserts a lone equals sign without words.
translations.idiomatic: Another equals-sign artifact in the text.

sentences.zh: 孟嘉

translations.literal: Meng Jia.
translations.idiomatic: Biography: Meng Jia.

translations.literal: The edition inserts a lone equals sign without words.
translations.idiomatic: Another equals-sign spacer.

sentences.zh: 孟嘉字萬年，江夏鄳人，吳司空宗曾孫也。

translations.literal: Meng Jia, styled Wannian, was a man of Meng in Jiangxia, great-great-grandson of Wu Minister of Works Zong.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Jia of Jiangxia traced his line to Wu's Meng Zong.

sentences.zh: 嘉少知名，太尉庾亮領江州，辟部廬陵從事。

translations.literal: Jia was known in youth; Grand Commandant Yu Liang held Jiang Province and summoned him as clerk for Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang made him a county clerk in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 嘉還都，亮引問風俗得失，對曰：「還傳當問吏。

translations.literal: When Jia returned to the capital, Liang led him in and asked gains and losses of local custom; he answered, "On return one should ask the clerks."
translations.idiomatic: Asked about Jiangxi, he said ask the bureaucrats.

sentences.zh: 」亮舉麈尾掩口而笑，謂弟翼曰：「孟嘉故是盛德人。

translations.literal: " Liang raised his fly-whisk to cover his mouth and laughed, telling younger brother Yi, "Meng Jia is indeed a man of abundant virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang laughed and called him a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 」轉勸學從事。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to clerk for promoting study.
translations.idiomatic: He became education officer.

sentences.zh: 褚裒時為豫章太守，正旦朝亮，裒有器識，亮大會州府人士，嘉坐次甚遠。

translations.literal: At the time Chu Pou was Administrator of Yuzhang; on New Year's dawn he paid court to Liang; Pou had capacity and insight; Liang held a great gathering of the province and prefecture worthies; Jia's seat was very far.
translations.idiomatic: At a New Year banquet Meng Jia sat far from the host.

sentences.zh: 裒問亮：「聞江州有孟嘉，其人何在？

translations.literal: Pou asked Liang, "I hear Jiang Province has a Meng Jia—where is the man?"
translations.idiomatic: Chu Pou asked where Meng Jia was.

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「在坐，卿但自覓。

translations.literal: " Liang said, "Among those seated—search for yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang said find him in the crowd.

sentences.zh: 」裒曆觀，指嘉謂亮曰：「此君小異，將無是乎？

translations.literal: " Pou looked over them all, pointed at Jia and told Liang, "This gentleman is a little unlike the rest—might it be he?"
translations.idiomatic: Chu Pou picked him out by presence.

sentences.zh: 」亮欣然而笑，喜裒得嘉，奇嘉為裒所得，乃益器焉。

translations.literal: " Liang smiled happily, pleased Pou had found Jia, marveling that Jia had been obtained by Pou, and esteemed him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang delighted in the pairing.

sentences.zh: 後為征西桓溫參軍，溫甚重之。

translations.literal: Afterwards he was clerk on the army of General Who Conquers the West Huan Wen; Wen greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen prized him on staff.

sentences.zh: 九月九日，溫燕龍山，僚佐畢集。

translations.literal: On the ninth day of the ninth month Wen feasted at Dragon Mountain; staff and aides all gathered.
translations.idiomatic: The Double Ninth banquet on Dragon Mountain.

sentences.zh: 時佐吏並著戎服，有風至，吹嘉帽墮落，嘉不之覺。

translations.literal: At the time adjutants all wore military dress; a wind came and blew Jia's cap off; Jia did not notice.
translations.idiomatic: Wind stole his hat; he never flinched.

sentences.zh: 溫使左右勿言，欲觀其舉止。

translations.literal: Wen told attendants not to speak, wishing to watch his bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen hushed the room to watch.

sentences.zh: 嘉良久如廁，溫令取還之，命孫盛作文嘲嘉，著嘉坐處。

translations.literal: After a long while Jia went to the privy; Wen ordered it fetched back for him, ordered Sun Sheng to compose a piece mocking Jia, and set it on Jia's seat.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen had the hat returned and Sun Sheng plant a satire on his cushion.

sentences.zh: 嘉還見，即答之，其文甚美，四坐嗟歎。

translations.literal: When Jia returned and saw it, he answered on the spot; the text was very fine; the four sides sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Jia replied in verse and silenced the table.

sentences.zh: 嘉好酣飲，愈多不亂。

translations.literal: Jia loved deep drinking—the more he drank, the less he stumbled.
translations.idiomatic: He drank heavily without losing composure.

sentences.zh: 溫問嘉：「酒有何好？

translations.literal: Wen asked Jia, "What is good about wine
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen asked what wine offered

sentences.zh: 而卿嗜之？

translations.literal: that you are so fond of it?"
translations.idiomatic: that could make him love it so much?"

sentences.zh: 」嘉曰：「公未得酒中趣耳。

translations.literal: " Jia said, "My lord has not yet got the taste within wine."
translations.idiomatic: Meng Jia said he had never tasted wine's true charm."

sentences.zh: 」又問：「聽妓，絲不如竹，竹不如肉，何謂也？

translations.literal: " He again asked, "They say listening to singing-girls—silk is not as good as bamboo, bamboo not as good as flesh—what does that mean?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked the old proverb on strings versus voice.

sentences.zh: 」嘉答曰：「漸近使之然。

translations.literal: " Jia answered, "It is gradual approach that makes it so."
translations.idiomatic: Meng Jia said each step closer to the human voice feels richer."

sentences.zh: 」一坐咨嗟。

translations.literal: " The whole company murmured praise.
translations.idiomatic: Guests murmured approval.

sentences.zh: 轉從事中郎，遷長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to clerk in service, promoted to chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to chief clerk on Huan Wen's staff.

sentences.zh: 年五十三卒於家。

translations.literal: At age fifty-three he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-three at home.

sentences.zh: :史臣曰：桓溫挺雄豪之逸氣，韞文武之奇才，見賞通人，夙標令譽。

translations.literal: The historiographers say: Huan Wen straightened a free spirit of heroic boldness, harbored rare talent in civil and military; he won praise from penetrating men and long bore fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: The historians: Huan Wen was a born warlord and scholar.

sentences.zh: 時既豺狼孔熾，疆場多虞，受寄捍城，用恢威略，乃逾越險阻，戡定岷峨，獨克之功，有可稱矣。

translations.literal: The age was then jackals and wolves fiercely blazing; the borders knew many alarms—entrusted with guarding the wall, he deployed awe-striking strategy; crossing peril and barrier, he pacified Min and Emei—the merit of conquering alone may be praised.
translations.idiomatic: He crushed Shu when the north was chaos.

sentences.zh: 及觀兵洛汭，修復五陵，引旆秦郊，威懷三輔，雖未能梟除凶逆，亦足以宣暢王靈。

translations.literal: When he displayed arms at the Luo River bend, repaired the five tombs, unfurled banners on Qin's outskirts, and overawed the three approaches—though he could not behead the fierce rebels, it still sufficed to proclaim royal numen.
translations.idiomatic: His Luoyang marches awed Guanzhong even in failure.

sentences.zh: 既而總戎馬之權，居形勝之地，自謂英猷不世，勳績冠時。

translations.literal: Then holding the power of war-horses, occupying terrain of advantage, he deemed his heroic plan unmatched in the age, his merit foremost of the times.
translations.idiomatic: Power went to his head.

sentences.zh: 挾震主之威，蓄無君之志，企景文而慨息，想處仲而思齊，睥睨漢廷，窺覦周鼎。

translations.literal: Bearing awe that shakes the ruler, harboring a mind without lord—he craned toward Emperor Wen of Jin and sighed, thought of Wang Dun and wished to match him, squinted at the Han court, spied the Zhou tripods.
translations.idiomatic: He envied Wang Dun and weighed the Han mandate.

sentences.zh: 復欲立奇功于趙魏，允歸望於天人；

translations.literal: Again he wished to win strange merit in Zhao and Wei, fulfill returned hope in heaven and men;
translations.idiomatic: He wanted northern triumph then the throne—

sentences.zh: 然後步驟前王，憲章虞夏。

translations.literal: then pace the former kings, take statutes from Yu and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: to walk as Shun and Yu.

sentences.zh: 逮乎石門路阻，襄邑兵摧，懟謀略之乖違，恥師徒之撓敗，遷怒於朝廷，委罪於偏裨，廢主以立威，殺人以逞欲，曾弗知寶命不可以求得，神器不可以力徵。

translations.literal: When Stone Gate was blocked and Xiangyi's troops were crushed, he resented strategy's going awry, shamed the army's frustration and defeat, shifted anger to the court, pinned blame on subordinate generals, deposed the ruler to display might, killed men to indulge desire—never knowing the precious mandate cannot be sought by cunning, the sacred regalia cannot be wrested by force.
translations.idiomatic: Fangtou broke him; he deposed an emperor and murdered to vent frustration—madness.

sentences.zh: 豈不悖哉！

translations.literal: Is it not contrary!
translations.idiomatic: What folly!

sentences.zh: 豈不悖哉！

translations.literal: Is it not contrary!
translations.idiomatic: What folly!

sentences.zh: 斯寶斧鋮之所宜加，人神之所同棄。

translations.literal: Therefore the executioner's axe should have fallen on him; men and gods alike would cast him off.
translations.idiomatic: He deserved the axe; heaven and earth rejected him.

sentences.zh: 然猶存極光寵，沒享哀榮，是知朝政之無章，主威之不立也。

translations.literal: Yet he still kept utmost glory in life and enjoyed mournful honor in death—this shows court governance lacked pattern and lordly awe was not established.
translations.idiomatic: Jin still buried him like a hero—proof the court had no spine.

translations.literal: 【Praise】
translations.idiomatic: Section marker: encomium.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：播越江濆，政弱權分。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Driven to the river's brink, government weak and power split.
translations.idiomatic: Praise: The court fled south, riven by strongmen.

sentences.zh: 元子悖力，處仲矜勳。

translations.literal: Yuanzi relied on brute force; Chuzhong boasted of merit.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen flexed muscle; Wang Dun flaunted victories.

sentences.zh: 跡既陵上，志亦無君。

translations.literal: Their tracks overbore the throne; their will acknowledged no lord.
translations.idiomatic: Both trampled their king and dreamed of supremacy.

sentences.zh: 罪浮浞，心窺舜禹。

translations.literal: Guilt floated past Zhuo; hearts peeped at Shun and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Their crime outdid ancient usurpers; their eyes coveted the mandate.

sentences.zh: 樹威外略，稱兵內侮。

translations.literal: They planted awe abroad and raised arms to insult the court within.
translations.idiomatic: They warred outside and bullied within.

sentences.zh: 惟身與嗣，竟罹齊斧。

translations.literal: Yet themselves and their heirs still met the executioner's axe.
translations.idiomatic: They and their sons still fell to the headsman.
